105. *Ṭa-ṭha* followed by *ṣa-ra-ama*. When *ṭa* or *ṭha* follow a word ending in *viṣṇu-pada*, there shall be the insertion of *ṣa-ra-ama*. And that [insertion] is preceded either by *viṣṇu-cakra* or *viṣṇu-cāpa*. *bhagavān + ṭīkate* = *bhagavāṃṣṭīkate*, *bhagavāṃṣṭīkate*. *bhagavān + ṭhakkuraḥ* = *bhagavāṃṣṭhakkuraḥ*, *bhagavāṃṣṭhakkuraḥ*.

106. *tathayoḥ* [followed by] *sarāmaḥ*. When *t* or *th* are followed by *s* or *r*, there shall be *ṣarāmaḥ*. And that [ṣ] is preceded by *viṣṇucakra* or preceded by *viṣṇucāpa*—*bhagavān + tarati* = *bhagavāṃstarati*, *bhagavāṃstarati*; *bhagavān + thūtkaroti* = *bhagavāṃsthūtkaroti*, *bhagavāṃsthūtkaroti*. ||106||
107. Not *tse*;

nor should *pare*, *narāmaḥ*, *viṣṇupadāntaḥ*, *viṣṇucakrapūrvaḥ*, or *viṣṇucāpapūrvaḥ* be followed by *sarāmaḥ*. [In these cases,] *bhagavān* is *sarūḥ*. In the case of *kān kān*, it should be stated as *kāṃskān* or it may remain as is. ||107||

108. Regarding *praśān*, at the beginning of [the following words], there is *hariveṇu* (the doubling of the consonant). For *praśān* ending in *viṣṇupada* (a word ending in a nasal), when followed by *cha*, *ṭa*, *ṭha*, *ta*, or *tha*, the *hariveṇu* (doubling) occurs according to the form of the subsequent letter: *praśān* + *caturbhujaḥ* = *praśāñcaturbhujaḥ*; *praśān* + *chādayati* = *praśāñchādayati*; *praśān* + *ṭīkate* = *praśāṇṭīkate*; *praśān* + *ṭhakkuraḥ* = *praśāṇṭhakkuraḥ*; *praśān* + *tarati* = *praśāntarati*. ||108||

109. Regarding *la-rāma*: when *le* follows, *la-rāma* preceded by *na-ra-āma* (i.e., *m*) becomes *la-rāma*. For example: *bhagavān līlāyate* = *bhagavāṃllīlāyate*. In this position, according to the rule that "the most similar [substitute] occurs," the *la-rāma* should indeed be nasalized (*sānunāsika*). For here, the *ya*, *va*, and *la* sounds are considered to be of two kinds: nasalized (*sānunāsika*) and non-nasalized (*niranunāsika*). ||109||

110. *ṇarāma* after *ḍ*, *ḍh*, and *ṇ*. When *ḍ*, *ḍh*, or *ṇ* follow a word ending in *narāma* (the suffix *am*), it becomes *ṇarāma*. — *garutmān* + *ḍayase* = *garutmaṇḍayase*; *cakrī* + *ḍhaukase* = *cakriṇḍhaukase*; *śārṅgī* + *ṇaṃ kuru* = *śārṅgiṇṇaṃ kuru*. ||110||

111. After *ja*, *jha*, *ña*, *śa*, or *ra*, there is *ña-ra-ama*. When *ña-ra-ama* follows *ja*, *jha*, *ña*, *śa*, or *ra*, it becomes *ñ-ra-ama*. *bhagavān jayati* = *bhagavāñjayati*. *bhagavān jhaṣarūpī* = *bhagavāñjhaṣarūpī*. *bhagavān ñuṅuve* = *bhagavāññuṅuve*. *bhagavān śūraḥ* = *bhagavāñ śūraḥ*. In the case of *chatva* (the substitution of *cha* for *śa*), it is *bhagavāñchūraḥ*. 111.

112. Or, when followed by *ś*, *r*, *ṣ*, *s*, *ant* (the end of a word), or *v*, the nasalization (*ñarāma*) may optionally occur at the end of *narāma* (words ending in *n*), *viṣṇupada* (words ending in *m*), or *carāmānta* (words ending in *c*). For example, *bhagavān śūraḥ* becomes *bhagavāñcśūraḥ*, *bhagavāñśūraḥ*, or, with the substitution of *ch* for *ś*, *bhagavāñcchūraḥ*. ||112||

113. Regarding *viṣṇucakra*: [the rule applies] when followed by a word denoting a devotee of Viṣṇu (*viṣṇujana*). When followed by a word other than a devotee of Viṣṇu, it is *marāma* (i.e., the sandhi does not apply). In the case of a subsequent word that is a devotee of Viṣ�ṇu, there should be *viṣṇucakra*. For example: *kṛṣṇaṃ smarati* = *viṣṇucakra* (because, according to worldly usage, the upper half of the *viṣṇucakra* moves forward), thus: *kṛṣṇaṃ smarati*. However, when followed by something other than a devotee of Viṣṇu, it is not so: *kṛṣṇaṃ + iccha* = *kṛṣṇamiccha*. Why was it said, "kṛṣṇagumñuṅuve"? This was done for the sake of establishing the proposition that "an unestablished form must not be discarded. Although it would have been appropriate to do this right there, it was not done. Therefore, because it was not done there, it is not *viṣṇucakra*. ||113||
114. For the word *viṣṇucakra*, [the elision occurs] before *hariveṇu* or before a member of the *viṣṇu* group; however, for that which ends in *viṣṇupada*, it is optional.

The *hariveṇu* [anusvāra] should occur after a word ending in *viṣṇu* when followed by a consonant belonging to the *viṣṇu*-group (*ka*, *ca*, *ṭa*, *ta*, *pa*), provided that the following word is not itself the word *viṣṇu*. However, there is an option (*vikalpa*) when the following word ends in *viṣṇu*. An example where the following word does not end in *viṣṇu* will be stated later (e.g., *gantā*, *mantā*, etc.). Examples include: *kṛṣṇaṃ kīrtayati* or *kṛṣṇaṅkīrtayati*; *kṛṣṇaṃ bhajati* or *kṛṣṇambhajati*; *saṃsāraṃ tarati* or *saṃsārantarati*. In these cases, it must be stated that the *sa* and *ra* [of the preceding word] do not undergo elision (*sarāmaniṣedha*). Why "in the *viṣṇu*-group"? Consider: *saṃvatsaraḥ*. (114)
115. And in the case of *yava* syllables, they consider the form of Viṣṇu’s bow to be the opposite.
The year is completed; it is fully measured; it cuts down completely. ||115||

116. After *sarveśvara*, even when it does not end in the word *padam*, the suffix *cha* (which becomes *īya*) is doubled. Thus, after *sarveśvara*, the suffix *cha* (as *īya*) becomes doubled: *kṛṣṇa* + *chatram* = *kṛṣṇacchatram*.
117. After *viṣṇupada* or *trivikrama*, the following *charāma* becomes double (i.e., *cha*) optionally: *yamunāchāyā* or *yamunācchāyā*.
118. After *āṅ* and *māṅ*, [the root] *ścar* is always doubled. The nasal *ṅ* of *ścar* is not employed: *ācchādayati*, *mācchidat*. 118.
119. After *vāman*, *ṅ*, *ṇ*, and *n* are doubled before *sarveśvara*.

When *sarveśvara* follows, *ṅ*, *ṇ*, and *n* occurring after *vāman* and ending in the word *viṣṇupada* are doubled: *paryaṅ + anantaḥ* = *paryaṅṅanantaḥ*; *sugaṇ + anantaḥ* = *sugaṇṇanantaḥ*; *kurvan + asti* = *kurvannasti*. ||119||
120. Regarding the term *viṣṇujana*: it may optionally remain as *viṣṇujana* when followed by *viṣṇujana*, but not when followed by *hari*.
After *vāmana*, *viṣṇujana* may optionally be doubled when followed by another *viṣṇujana*, but it is not doubled when followed by *hari*—as in *dadhyupendrasya* or *daddhyupendrasya*.

121. From Harimitra comes Viṣṇugaṇa; from Viṣṇugaṇa comes Harimitra; from Śauri comes Sātvata; and from Sātvata comes Śauri again—thus it should be stated twice, or rather, "in all cases, [the name] Īśvara.

[The forms] Yamunalkkārāyate, dadhyupendrasya, bhagavāṃścchādayati, and suvākśśaureḥ occur here; even the *cha*-sandhi is not accepted in these instances. In other cases, it follows the previous rule. ||121||

122. After *rarāmāt*, [the word] *sarveśvara* occurs, except for *harigotra*. After *rarāmāt*, there may be *viṣṇujana*; after *viṣṇujana*, there may be *para*, or it may occur twice. After *sarveśvara*, however, except for *harigotra*—there may be *haryāsana* or *haryāsana*, or *kārṣṇa* or *kārṣṇa*. ||122||
123. It must be stated that [the Supreme] is higher than the Lord of All (*sarveśvara*).

From the state that is higher than the Lord of All, the class of Viṣṇu may be either double or single—namely, Brahmā or Brahman. Here, however, it is not so; for what is the reference (*parāmarśa*) in the passage beginning with "But in the Lord of All," etc.? It refers to those whose manifestation is purposeless (*vyarthabhānavya*); [he] is worthy [of it]. ||123||

124. But [the suffix] *ha* is not used after the word *viṣṇujan*. It is stated [in the rule]: "after *viṣṇujan*" (*Saṃskṛtaprakāśa* 120), etc., in the section on duality; however, the fact that the alternative view regarding non-duality—namely, "in all cases, when there is totality"—is not mentioned therein is an error. ||124||

125. Regarding the non-appearance of *viṣṇujanāt* before *viṣṇudāsasya*, and [the appearance] when *viṣṇudāsaḥ* is in the same word-group (*savarga*): there may be the non-appearance of *viṣṇujanāt* before a subsequent *viṣṇudāsaḥ* when *viṣṇudāsaḥ* is in the same word-group—as in *bhagavāñcchūraḥ* or *bhagavāñchūraḥ*. Its omission in the preceding rule is because it is not mandatory due to being optional. ||125||

126. In the case of words that imitate inarticulate sounds (*avyaktānukaraṇa*), the syllable *it* is substituted for the final portion [of the sound], and the substitution of *hari* is prohibited. Thus: *paṭat* becomes *paṭiti*; *ghaṭat* becomes *ghaṭiti*. ||126||
127. Not [the case] regarding the state of being the Lord of all;
*srāt* means *sraditi*. ||127||
128. When a word is repeated twice or thrice, the final [consonant] is not doubled; however, for the penultimate [consonant], it is optional.

Thus, *paṭatpaṭat* becomes either *paṭatpaṭad* or *paṭatpaṭe*. How is it that *baḍabhī* becomes *valabhī*, *paryaṅkaḥ* becomes *palyaṅkaḥ*, *raghuḥ* becomes *laghuḥ*, and *kapirikā* becomes *kapilikā*, and so forth? This is because the sounds of *ḍa* and *la*, as well as *ra* and *la*, are generally heard as identical.
129. It should be stated that *ṭu* is substituted for *ṭan* after a word ending in *r*.
Thus: *ṣaṭ sādhavaḥ* becomes *ṣaṭtsādhavaḥ*; *bhagavān sādhuḥ* becomes *bhagavāntsādhuḥ*. ||129||
130. It should be stated that when followed by *ś* (the sibilant) or *r*, the letters *ṇ* and *n* optionally take the augment *ṭ* and *k* respectively.
Thus: *sugaṇ* + *śaṅkaraḥ* = *sugaṇṭśaṅkaraḥ*; *prāṅ* + *svabhūḥ* = *prāṅksvabhūḥ*; *prāṅ* + *ṣaṣṭhaḥ* = *prāṅkṣaṣṭhaḥ*. ||130||
Thus ends the section on the alliance with the followers of Viṣṇu.

Now, the junction concerning the *viṣṇusarga* (the visarga): 131. The *viṣṇusarga* before *ka* and *kha* may optionally become the *jihvāmūlīya*. The *viṣṇusarga* preceding *ka* and *kha* may optionally become the *jihvāmūlīya*. This is a specific phoneme produced at the root of the tongue, written with the shape of a thunderbolt (*vajra*). According to the world (*loka*), it moves upward like the *viṣṇujan* (the *visarga*). The same applies to the *upadhmānīya*. Examples: *kaḥ kṛṣṇaḥ* or *ka ṃ kṛṣṇaḥ*; *kṛṣṇaḥ khelati* or *kṛṣṇa ṃ khelati*. ||131||

132. The Upadhmānīya occurs before *p* and *ph*. When followed by *p* or *ph*, the Visarga may optionally become the Upadhmānīya. This is a specific phonetic element produced at the lips, written in the shape of an elephant's frontal globe (*gajakumbha*). For example: *kṛṣṇaḥ paramaḥ* or *kṛṣṇaḥ? paramaḥ*; *kṛṣṇaḥ phalam* or *kṛṣṇaḥ? phalam*. ||132||
133. Not [the substitution] occurs when *śauri* is followed by those [consonants].

When *śauri* is followed by those [consonants], namely *ka*, *kha*, *pa*, or *pha*, the *viṣṇusarga* (visarga) in the position of the *jihvāmūlīya* and so forth shall not occur. For example: *kṛṣṇaḥ kṣīrasyati*, *kṛṣṇaḥ psāti*. In these cases, the operations pertaining to compounds (*samāsa*) and the *ṣatva* (substitution of *ṣ*) will be explained later (Samāsapradīpikā 325), as in *niṣkṛṣṇaḥ* and *rakṣaspāśaḥ*.
134. *śarām* after *cha* and *cha*. When *cha* and *cha* follow, *śarām* shall occur. *kṛṣṇaḥ* + *carati* = *kṛṣṇaścarati*; *kṛṣṇaḥ* + *chādayati* = *kṛṣṇaśchādayati*. ||134||
135. *ṣatvam* after *ṭa* and *ṭha*. When *ṭa* or *ṭha* follow, there is the substitution of *ṣa* for *sa*. Thus: *kṛṣṇaḥ* + *ṭīkate* = *kṛṣṇaṣṭīkate*; *kaḥ* + *ṭharāmaḥ* = *kaṣṭharāmaḥ*. ||135||

136. *Sarāmaḥ* occurs after *t* and *th*. When *t* and *th* are followed by [the letter *r*], *sarāmaḥ* (the insertion of *s*) shall occur. *kṛṣṇaḥ* + *tarati* = *kṛṣṇastarati*; *kṛṣṇaḥ* + *thūtkaroti* = *kṛṣṇasthūtkaroti*. ||136||
137. Not "tse.
What is the handle? ||137||

138. Regarding the *śauri* [suffixes], there may be *śauri*, or [the following]: when *viṣṇusarga* follows *śauri*, or when another [suffix] follows, that same letter may remain unchanged—e.g., *kṛṣṇaḥ śaraṇam* or *kṛṣṇaśśaraṇam*; *hareḥ ṣaṇḍaḥ* or *hareṣṣaṇḍaḥ*; *hareḥ surabhiḥ* or *haressurabhiḥ*. ||136||

139. In the case of *sātvataparatva*, [the visarga] is also to be elided. When *sātvata* follows those [words], as in the case of *śauri* followed by another word, the *viṣṇusarga* (visarga) may optionally be elided—thus: *hareḥ sthalam* becomes either *hare sthalam* or *hares sthalam*. ||139||
140. [The *visarga*] of *ur* (the word *u*) remains unchanged before *ā*, *rāma*, and *gopāla*.

After *arāma*, there is the substitution of *viṣṇusarga* (the *visarga* of Viṣṇu), which becomes *urāma*. When *arāma* and *gopāla* follow—*kṛṣṇaḥ* + *atra* = *kṛṣṇo'tra*; *kṛṣṇaḥ* + *gacchati* = *kṛṣṇo gacchati*. However, this does not apply when *mahāpuruṣa* follows due to the specific mention of *arāma*: *āgaccha tīrthaśravā3 atra*. The elision of the *viṣṇusarga* will be explained later. ||140||

141. The Visarga following the words *bhoḥ*, *bhagoḥ*, and *aghoḥ*—provided they are not followed by *a* or *ā*—is to be elided; however, when followed by *sarveśvara*, the *ya* [of *yaḥ*] is also elided, and there is no euphonic combination (*sandhi*) in the case of an elision.
That is to say, the Visarga of *viṣṇuḥ* (the Visarga-sarga) following the two vowels *a* and *ā*, as well as the words *bhoḥ*, *bhagoḥ*, and *aghoḥ*, should be elided.

Regarding the two supreme forms, *sarveśvara* and *gopāla*: in the case of the supreme *sarveśvara*, when the *ya-ra-ama* [substitution] occurs, there shall be no further *sandhi* once that [substitute] has been elided—for example, *kṛṣṇaḥ + iha* may become either *kṛṣṇa iha* or *kṛṣṇayiha*; *kṛṣṇāḥ + atra* may become either *kṛṣṇā atra* or *kṛṣṇāyatra*; *bhoḥ + ananta* may become either *bho ananta* or *bhoyananta*; *bhagoḥ + ananta* may become either *bhago ananta* or *bhagoyananta*; and *aghoḥ + avaiṣṇava* may become either *agho avaiṣṇava* or *aghoyavaiṣṇava*.

In this context, after *advaya*, the *yarāma* (the *r*-sandhi resulting in *ry*) should be understood as being slightly touched (*īṣatsparśī*) and even more slightly touched (*īṣatsparśitarah*). After *orāma* (the *r* following *o*), however, it is only slightly touched. In *gopāle na yarāmaḥ*—as in "Kṛṣṇa is coming," "O Govinda," "Bhago Govinda," or "Agho Harivimukha"—[the rule does not apply]. He states [the exceptions] due to specific injunctions regarding *ādarāma* and *gopāla*: "Kṛṣṇa here," "Kṛṣṇa is coming. In the case of *saiṣa* for metrical completion: *saḥ* + *eṣaḥ* = *sa eṣaḥ*. "This very Rāma, son of Daśaratha"; "this very King Yudhiṣṭhira."
This very Karna is a man of great renunciation; this very Bhima is possessed of great strength.

142. *eṣa* and *sa*: When followed by a word denoting Viṣṇu (*viṣṇujana*), the suffixes *eṣa* derived from the word *etad* and *sa* derived from the word *tad* are subject to elision. When a word denoting Viṣṇu follows, the [suffixes] of *eṣa* and *sa* are dropped. For example: *eṣaḥ* + *kṛṣṇaḥ* = *eṣa kṛṣṇaḥ*; *saḥ* + *rāmaḥ* = *sa rāmaḥ*. ||142||
143. But [the suffix *ka*] does not apply after a negative compound (*nañ-samāsa*) or after the word *eṣa*.

Examples: *aneṣaḥ kṛṣṇaḥ*, *aso rāmaḥ*, *eṣakaḥ kṛṣṇaḥ*, *sako rāmaḥ*. Because of its association with the word *saḥ*, [the suffix does not apply] after the verbal root *iṣ* (to seek) in the form *eṣa*; thus, one says *eṣo bhavati*. ||143||

144. After *īśvara*, [the elision of *s* occurs] before *sarveśvara* and *gopāla*. After *īśvara*, the *visarga* (*ra*) of *viṣṇu* becomes *rarāmaḥ*. After the subsequent [words] *sarveśvara* and *gopāla*: *hareḥ* + *idam* = *hareridam*; *hariḥ* + *gacchati* = *harirgacchati*. ||144||
145. *Rarāma* is also derived from *anīśvara*.

If that very *viṣṇusarga* (the creation of Viṣṇu) were born from *rarāma*, then *rarāma* would be superior even to *īśvara* and *anīśvara*—being higher than both the Lord of All (*sarveśvara*) and Gopāla. Examples: *prātaḥ* + *atra* = *prātaratra*; *gīḥ* + *mukundasya* = *gīrmukundasya*; *bhrātaḥ* + *vraje* = *bhrātarvraje*; *bhrātaḥ* + *govindaṃ paśya* = *bhrātargovindaṃ paśya*. ||145||

146. In place of *viṣṇusarga* (the visarga following *ahnaḥ*) before words other than *rātri*, *rūpa*, and *rathantara*, it becomes *r*. Before words other than *rātri*, *rūpa*, and *rathantara*, the *r* occurs in place of the *viṣṇusarga* of *ahnaḥ*: *ahnaḥ* + *ahnaḥ* = *aharahas*; *ahnaḥ* + *gaṇaḥ* = *ahargaṇaḥ*. This applies only before *sarveśvara* and *gopāla*. Not here: *aharpatiḥ*. But not before *rātri* and so on: *ahorātriḥ*. That which is modified in one part is not different from the original: *ahorātraḥ*. *ahorūpam*. *ahorathantaraṃ sāma*. ||146||

147. *ro* is elided when followed by *ra*, and the preceding [vowel] becomes *trivikrama*. When *ra* follows *rarāma*, it should be elided; the vowel preceding *rarāma* becomes *vāmana* and [the following *ra*] becomes *trivikrama*. *bhrātaḥ + rāmānujaṃ paśya* = *bhrātā rāmānujaṃ paśya* (O brother, see Rāmānuja). *hariḥ + rādhāpriyaḥ* = *harī rādhāpriyaḥ* (Hari, the beloved of Rādhā).
Thus ends the section on the creation of Viṣṇu.
Thus ends the first chapter, on Nouns and Sandhi, in the Vaiṣṇava grammar titled *Śrī-Śrī-Saṃkṣepa-Harināmāmṛta*. ||1||
The entire state of that Viṣṇu, who alone is the substratum of all forms as well as all names,
is described through devotion to Viṣṇu.

Now, regarding those "Viṣṇu-steps" which are born from names—that is, those steps of Viṣṇu that have arisen by way of names—they will be described hereafter. 1. A name possessing meaning is one characterized by devotion to the Viṣṇu who is not a verbal root (adhātu).

The roots beginning with *bhū* and *asan* are verbal roots (*dhātu*). Those beginning with *svādi* and *tibi* are the devotional modes of Viṣṇu (*viṣṇubhakti*); the ancients call them "inflections" (*vibhakti*). Excluding those roots and those devotional modes, whatever form of word is associated with a meaning, that shall be designated as a "name" (*nāman*). Some say it is "gender" (*liṅga*); others say it is a "nominal stem" (*prātipadika*). And those meanings are substance (*dravya*), quality (*guṇa*), genus (*jāti*), and action (*kriyā*). The meaning is: that form of word which is associated with [one of] those [meanings] and denotes them. (1) Substance (*dravya*) is every entity, beginning from "behold the animal" up to "clay.
(2) Quality (*guṇa*) is the property residing in that [substance], such as sovereignty and so forth, or sound, touch, and so forth.
(3) *Jāti* (genus) is the state of being common, such as Brahminhood, cowness, and so forth.

(4) *Kriyā* (action) is the meaning of a verbal root (*dhātvartha*), such as existence, taking food, knowledge, dwelling, and so on. Because of the requirement that [the item] must have meaning (*arthavat*), in cases such as "kṛṣṇa" and the like, each individual syllable would not possess the status of a name (*nāmatva*). This also applies to the case of "gavityayamāha. ||1||
2. The base form (*prakṛti*) comes first;
it is twofold, distinguished as nouns (*nāman*) and verbal roots (*dhātu*). ||2||
3. The suffix (pratyaya) is of four kinds, distinguished as verbal roots (dhātu), finite verbs (ākhyāta), primary derivatives (kṛt), and secondary derivatives (taddhita). ||3||
4. Among those, for the masculine [nouns]: *su* and *au* [take] *jas*;
*am* and *au* [take] *śas*; *ṭā*, *bhyām*, and *bhis*; *ṅe*, *bhyām*, and *bhyas*; *ṅasi*, *bhyām*, and *bhyas*; *ṅas*, *os*, and *ām*; *ṅi*, *os*, and *sup*.

These twenty-one suffixes beginning with *su* are the case-endings (*viṣṇubhakti*) of Viṣṇu; each should follow the noun. Among them: *su*, *au*, and *jas* are the first case (*prathamā*); *am*, *au*, and *śas* are the second case (*dvitīyā*); *ṭā*, *bhyām*, and *bhis* are the third case (*tṛtīyā*); *ṅe*, *bhyām*, and *bhyas* are the fourth case (*caturthī*); *ṅasi*, *bhyām*, and *bhyas* are the fifth case (*pañcamī*); *ṅas*, *os*, and *ām* are the sixth case (*ṣaṣṭhī*); and *ṅi*, *os*, and *sup* are the seventh case (*saptamī*).

Here, one should understand that for the first [case], the singular is *su*, the dual is *au*, and the plural is *jas*; for the second, the singular is *am*, the dual is *au*, and the plural is *śas*, and so forth. These are called "the *svādi* suffixes," while others call them "the *syādi* suffixes. Some call them "the *sup* suffixes. (4)

5. Regarding *jaṭaśaṅapā* (the clusters of consonants): *it*, *uṃśca*, *soṃ*, *ṅasiḥ*, and *ric*. That which goes (*eti*), moves (*gacchati*), or does not remain (*na tiṣṭhati*) is called an *it* and an *anubandha*. It serves for the purpose of pronunciation, as a marker, and sometimes as a cause for grammatical rules (*vidhi*) and so forth. These [consonants] are *its* in the following cases: in the teaching of established forms (*siddhopadeśa*), in the case of Viriñci, and in the presence of Viṣṇu and Cāpasaveśvara; the final [consonant] in the word *viṣṇujana* in expressions such as *atit*; in the presence of *āṅ*, *māṅ*, *uñ*, and *nañ*; in the case of Viriñci in certain instances; the *iṭ*, *uṭ*, and *ūṭ* at the beginning of verbal roots; the *jaṭaṇas* at the beginning of suffixes; the *śavarga* (the *śa*-group) when not followed by a *taddhita* suffix; and that [cluster] in the devotion to Viṣṇu, which is equal to the body (*tanusama*).

The Siddhopadeśas, which consist of verbal roots, suffixes, and Viṣṇus (the vowels), along with the various divisions such as the *arāma* and others, together with the Viṣṇucāpas (the consonants), are called the Vaidikas. ||5||
6. Nouns are of four kinds:
masculine, such as *puruṣottama*; feminine, such as *lakṣmī*; neuter, such as *brahman*; and genderless, such as indeclinables (*avyaya*). ||6||

In that context, all [names] ending in "īśvara" have the form of Puruṣottama; therein, the word "kṛṣṇa" ends in "rāma. Thus, when "kṛṣṇasum" is established in the nominative singular, the syllable "u" is for the purpose of pronunciation.
7. The *viṣṇupada* [substitution] is established by devotion to Viṣṇu.
A form derived from a nominal stem or a verbal root, established through devotion to Viṣṇu, shall be designated as a *viṣṇupada*. The ancients [use the term] "pada. ||7||
From that point onward, his procedure should be like the flow of the Ganges;
for where no limiting adjunct exists, the subsequent does not arise before the preceding.
8. *Sararāmayor viṣṇusargo viṣṇupadānte*.
In the place of *sara* and *rāma*, there shall be the substitution of *viṣṇu*, provided that the word *viṣṇu* follows at the end [of the compound]. For example: *kṛṣṇaviṣṇuḥ*.
Thus, the rule is stated first and then the commentary (*vṛtti*), for fear of excessive prolixity.
However, it is done in such a way that the meaning may be established by the sūtra itself.
And for the sake of the sequence of the means of accomplishment (*sādhana*), it is not set forth as a governing rule (*adhikāra*);
otherwise, a different procedure would have to be sought to awaken the ignorant.
First the cause, then the effect, and then the effect caused by another;
this sequence should generally be stated throughout all the sūtras.
And in sequence, the fifth, first, and likewise the seventh [case-endings are used];
in some instances, the locative of domain (*viṣayasaptamī*) occurs in place of a subsequent cause.
When preceded by the word *kārya*, the fifth case (*pañcamī*) should be used; however, in the place of *kārya*, the sixth case (*ṣaṣṭhī*) is used.
When *kārya* itself is the object, the first case (*prathamā*) should be expressed, while the seventh case (*saptamī*) is used when another term meaning "object" (*viṣaya*) follows.
In some cases, the accusative case is desired after the word *vinā* for the purpose of negation,
where there is an impossibility of all the constituent parts [of a rite], yet only a few minor parts are present.
Therefore, for the sake of the understanding of children, having broken off a piece from the top [of the staff],
marks should be placed on all the threads according to the sūtras, in order to manifest devotion to Viṣṇu.

For example, in the case of *sararāmayoḥ*, *kāryasthāna* (the locus of the operation) is [the context]; *viṣṇusargaḥ* is the *kārya* (the operation); and that which ends with *viṣ* is the *viṣaya* (the domain). Here, there is neither a subsequent cause (*paranimitta*) nor a preceding cause (*pūrvanimitta*). For instance: in the rule *idvayameva yaḥ sarveśvare* (Saṃkṣiptasāraprakriyā 59), *sarveśvaraḥ* is the subsequent cause; then, in *śaścho vā* (Saṃkṣiptasāraprakriyā 99), *viṣṇudāsaḥ* is the preceding cause. However, in cases such as *viṣṇujane* (Saṃkṣiptasāraprakriyā 120) and *harau vinā*, those two [causes] are prohibited.

Thus, in the nominative singular, *kṛṣṇaḥ*. In the dual, *kṛṣṇa* + *au*; by *odvaye au* (Sārasvataprakriyā 57), [it becomes] *kṛṣṇau*. In the plural, *kṛṣṇa* + *jas*; the *j* is for the sake of marking [the case-ending], to indicate the distinction from *śas* and the others. The same applies hereafter. The two forms of Viṣṇu, Trivikrama and Sarga—[in the plural]: *kṛṣṇāḥ*. ||8||

In the second case, *kṛṣṇa* + *am*. 9. *Daśāvatārādaṃ śasos rāmaharaḥ*: [The rule] "the elision of *ra* and *ma* after *daśāvatāra*" applies here. Thus, *kṛṣṇam*. This [mention of] *hara* (elision) indicates that even the elision of something other than a suffix-form cause is a "great elision" (*mahāhara*). Therefore, because it is caused solely by a single element (*ekātmaka*), *trivikrama* does not apply. In the dual of the second case, *kṛṣṇa* + *au* = *kṛṣṇau*. In the plural, as before, *kṛṣṇa* + *śas*; since *śas* is marked with *ś* (*śit*), there is the elision of *ra* and *ma*. "That which is modified in one part is not different [from the original]" (*ekadeśavikṛtamananyavat*); the meaning is that it remains the very same name. ||8||
And from that:
10. *Trivikrama* is the moon for the ten incarnations; therefore, he is among us in the masculine form. *Ā* is for the purpose of pronunciation, [and] *kṛṣṇān*. 9.
In the case of the third person singular, the suffix is *ṭā*: 11. That which ends in *ar* is designated as *kṛṣṇa*. 12. After *kṛṣṇa*, the suffix *ṭā* becomes *ina*.

By the force of the rule "ṭā," the genitive case ending is elided; the absence of sandhi is for the sake of clarity. The same applies elsewhere. Thus: *kṛṣṇa* + *ina*; by [the rule] "advayamidvaye e" (Saṃkṣiptasāra-prakriyā 48), it becomes *kṛṣṇena*. ||12||
In the dual case, *kṛṣṇa* + *bhyām*—13. For Kṛṣṇa, there is Trivikrama [substitution] before the suffix *gopāle*.
A rule consisting of a single phoneme applies at the end: *kṛṣṇābhyām*. ||13||
In the plural, *kṛṣṇa* + *bhis* becomes *kṛṣṇair-bhis*.
According to rule 14, when there is a double [suffix] beginning with *ai*, the *viṣṇu-sarga* (the insertion of *r*) occurs: thus, *kṛṣṇaiḥ* ||14||
In the case of the fourth case in the singular: 15. *kṛṣṇāt* becomes *kṛṣṇāya*. *kṛṣṇasya trivikramaḥ* (Viṣṇu Purāṇa 13) = *kṛṣṇāya*. In the dual: *kṛṣṇābhyām*. ||15||
In the plural, *bhyas*—16. After *kṛṣṇa*, when it refers to Viṣṇu, in the plural:
*kṛṣṇebhyaḥ*. ||16||

In the singular of the fifth case, *kṛṣṇa* + *bhis* [becomes] *kṛṣṇaiḥ*. From *kṛṣṇa*, after the suffix *ṭā* (fifth case singular), *āt* is substituted: *kṛṣṇāt*. In the dual and plural of the fifth case, it is like the fourth case: *kṛṣṇābhyām*, *kṛṣṇebhyaḥ*. ||17||
In the singular sixth case, *kṛṣṇa* + *ṅas*: 18. *ṅasi* becomes *sya*. *kṛṣṇasya*. ||18||
In the case of duality, [the suffix] *os* follows:
19. *e* replaces [the final vowel of] *kṛṣṇa* before *osi*. By *e ay* (Pāṇini 6.1.78), [we get] *kṛṣṇayoḥ*. ||19||
In the case of plurality, [the suffix] *ām* is applied: 20. After *vāmana*, *gopī*, and *rādhā*, the augment *nuṭ* is added before *ām*.

Such is the rule for Viṣṇu. The augments *uṭ* and *āṭ* are elided. An augment marked with *ṭ* (ṭit) is related to the subsequent element; an augment marked with *k* (kit) is related to the preceding element. ||20||

21. In that regard, in all instances where *ṭi* is measured [as short], the augmentations (*āgama*) apply everywhere except for *śnam*; this is the *ugantakicca*. For example: *nuk*, *puk*, *tuk*, *ghuk*, and so forth. Then, when *nāmi* is present: ||21||

22. For *vāmana*, the name is *trivikrama*; for the word *nṛ*, however, it is *tu-vā*, but not for the [names of the] Kṛṣṇas. Although [the form] *kṛṣṇasya trivikramaḥ* (Vi.Pra. 13) is established by this very rule, the purpose of the sūtra is [to apply it] specifically in cases such as *harīṇām* (Vi.Pra. 36). In the singular locative (*saptamy-ekavacane*), from *kṛṣṇaṅi*: [the suffixes] *ṅ*, *it*, and *e* [are applied]; according to *advayamidvaye e* (Sa.Pra. 48), we have *kṛṣṇe*. In the dual locative (*dvitve os*), we have *kṛṣṇayoḥ*. ||20||
In the plural, *sup* [is applied]; *parāma* is *it*; *kṛṣṇasya* is *e* (Viṣṇupurāṇa 16)—23.

After *īśvara*, *hari*, *mitra*, and *kaṅa*, the *ṣatva* of the suffix *viriñci* occurs even when there is an intervention by *num* and *viṣṇusarga*, but not for those ending in *viṣṇupada* or beginning with *sāti*. Examples:
*kṛṣṇeṣu*. 23.
Now, regarding the vocative case: therein, the word *he* indicates the vocative.
24. In the vocative, [the suffix] is termed *sur* and *sambuddhi*. And it is called "sambuddhi. ||24||

25. Non-occurrence of the vocative case for the Buddha. O Kṛṣṇa! [In] the dual and plural, it is as before: O Kṛṣṇau! O Kṛṣṇāḥ! Here, only the nominative case [ending] applies. Even in the absence of the word *he* (vocative particle)—as in *kṛṣṇa*, *kṛṣṇau*, *kṛṣṇāḥ*—there is no transgression of its being a name (*nāman*), because the meaning is still covered by that [name]. Consequently, in cases such as *kṛṣṇa yāsi* (O Kṛṣṇa, you go) or *kṛṣṇa bhāsi* (O Kṛṣṇa, you shine), the specific grammatical forms prescribed for names, such as *trivikrama* and so on, would not apply. Likewise: *rāmaḥ*, *rāmau*, *rāmāḥ*, etc. 25.

26. After two *ra* sounds or *ṣa* sounds, the *ṇa* [substitution] occurs for the following *na*, even when there is an intervention by *sa*, *eśvara*, *ha*, *ṣa*, or the *ka*-group or *pa*-group, provided it is in the same word (*samānapada*) and not at the end of the word "viṣṇupada."

*rāmān*, *rāmeṇa*, and so forth. Vāmana, Nārāyaṇa, Govinda, Vaikuṇṭha, Vāsudeva, and others also end in *arāma* and are treated like *kṛṣṇa*. In forms such as *kurvann asti*, there is no substitution of *ṇ* for the preceding *rāma* when there is a doubling [of the suffix], because that is not prescribed therein. The word *a* also ends in *arāma* by the maxim "in a single entity, the beginning and the end are as if one"; thus: *aḥ*, *au*, *āḥ*, and so forth. Regarding the vocative, it is desired to be non-obligatory (*anitya*) elsewhere; thus: *he a* or *a he*.
In calling from a distance, the status of a Great Person (*mahāpuruṣatva*) is held to belong only to *hai* and *hayo*; thus: *he a3* or *a he3*. (26)
27. The group beginning with *śas* is designated as *yadu*.
28. In this context, for these words—*pāda*, *danta*, *māsa*, and *yuṣ*—the forms *pad*, *dat*, *mās*, and *ūṣ* are used; they are *viriñci* [substitutes] or belong to the *yadu* class.

"Enumeration according to order" (*yathāsaṅkhyam-anudeśaḥ*) means that when there is an equal number of similar bases (*prakṛti*) and suffixes (*pratyaya*), as well as similar operations (*kārya*) to be applied, the rule of application occurs according to their respective order. That is to say, the first [element] corresponds to the first, the second to the second, and so forth. Furthermore, the forms should be understood in this context as ending in *viṣṇujana*, for example: *padaḥ* (from the feet), *pādān* (the feet), *padā* (by the foot), *pādena* (with the foot), *padbhyām* (by two feet), *pādābhyām* (with two feet), and so on.
Now, regarding the nature of the nominal stem (dhātu): *viśvapā* ends in *ār*. [The forms are: *viśvapāḥ*, *viśvapau*, *viśvapāḥ*; [the accusative plural is] *viśvapām*, *viśvapau*. ||28||
*Viśvapāśas*—29. [The forms] *ārāmaharaḥ*, *yadusarveśvaraḥ*, and *na tvāpaḥ* are not included. *Viśvapāḥ*: *viśvapāṭ*, *ṭ* = *viśvapā*, *viśvapābhyām*, *viśvapābhiḥ*.
viśvapāṅe, ṅi = viśvape, viśvapābhyām, viśvapābhyaḥ.
*viśvapāṅ asi*, *iṅgāv*, *itau* = *viśvapaḥ*, *viśvapābhyām*, *viśvapābhyaḥ*.
viśvapāṅas becomes viśvapaḥ; [the forms] are viśvapoḥ and viśvapām.
viśvapāṅi = viśvapi, viśvapoḥ, viśvapāsu.

"He is Viśvapā," and so forth. In this manner, there are Somapā and the others. According to Kramadīśvara and others, the rule for the removal [of the suffix] applies to Hāhā, Abja, and the rest; thus, *hāhaḥ* means "from Hāhān," and *abjaḥ* means "from Abjān. Some maintain that *hāhāḥ* means "the Hāhās" and *abjāḥ* means "the Abjas. Similarly, there are Agregāḥ and Udadhikrāḥ. (27)
The word *hari* ending in *i* or *u* is termed *harisaṃjña*:
*agniḥ*, *ghiḥ*, and *hariḥ*. ||30||

31. *harita* and *au* [are] the *pūrvasavarṇa*. In the word *haritaḥ*, the suffix *tas* follows the fifth case (*pañcamī*), and it is a secondary derivative (*taddhita*); [the forms are] *hari* and *harī*. 31.
32. The single substitute for two *i*s is *e*; for two *u*s, *o*; for two *ṛ*s, *ar*; and for two *ṝ*s, *al*—these are designated as *govinda*.
They are also designated as *guṇa*.
33. Those ending in *ṅi* are designated as *vṛṣṇi*. 34. After *hari*, *govinda* is substituted [for the nominative plural marker] when followed by a *vṛṣṇi* or *buddha* [in the plural].
[Examples: *harayaḥ*; [accusative singular: *harim*; [nominative dual: *harī*; [accusative plural: *harīn*. ||34||
35. The nominative singular is *haritaṣṭā*, but not when [the word] means Lakṣmī;
[the forms are] *hariṇā*, *haribhyām*, *haribhiḥ*.
haraye, haribhyām, haribhyaḥ ||35||
36. After these two [stems], *ṅasi* and *ṅas* are replaced by *ara*. [Examples:
*hareḥ*, *haribhyām*, *haribhyaḥ*.
hareḥ, haryoḥ, harīṇām ||36||
37. After the root *hṛ*, [the suffix] *ṅe* becomes *au*;
thus, *harāmahe*. 37.
38. The final letters beginning with *sarva* and *īśvara* are designated as belonging to the world (*saṃsāra*). 39. The elision (*hara*) of the world occurs before the stem *cit*.

According to the ancients, this applies when the suffix begins with *ḍ*. [Examples: *harau*, *haryoḥ*, *hariṣu*. O *hare*! Similarly, [the declension of] *agni*, *ravi*, *kavi*, *giri*, and so forth. The word *tri* has all genders and ends in the plural; in the masculine: *trayaḥ*, *trīn*, *tribhiḥ*, *tribhyaḥ*, *tribhyaḥ*. ||39||

40. The word *traya* is used in the sense of itself (*svārtha*). [Examples: *trayāṇām*. Even when it occurs at the end of a compound—as in *paramatrayāṇām*—it retains this sense; however, when not in its own sense—as in *priyatrīṇām*—it does not. [Example for the locative: *triṣu*. ||40||

The word *kati* is treated in the same way: 41. After a numeral ending in *ṣaṇ*, and after *kati*, there is the elision (*mahāhara*) of the case-endings *jas* and *śas* in their own sense (*svārthe*). Here, due to absolute dissolution (*ātyantikalaya*), the grammatical operation of a suffix does not apply; thus, *govindaḥ* [is not formed]. Examples include *kati*, *kati*, *katibhiḥ*, and so forth. The mention of *kater* is an elliptical indication (*upalakṣaṇa*) for both *kati* and *yati*; this is because of such usage as *yati te nāga śīrṣāṇi* ("O Nāga, you have eight heads") and *tata te nāga vedanāḥ* ("Therefore, O Nāga, you have eight pains"). Similarly, one has *paramakati* and so on. However, when not in its own sense (*asvārthe*), one has *priyakatayaḥ*.
Now, regarding the word *sakhi* (friend):

42. After the words *ṛk*, *arāma*, and *sakhi*, as well as after *uśanas*, *purudaṃśas*, and *sanehas*, the suffix *āc* is applied in place of the nominative singular ending *su*, except for the word *buddha*. [Examples:
*saṃsārasya haraḥ* (the destroyer of saṃsāra). 42.

43. For a pair of *a*s, there is *ā*; for a pair of *i*s, *ai*; for a pair of *u*s, *au*; for a pair of *ṛ*s, *ār*; for a pair of *ṝ*s, *āl*. This is designated as "vṛṣṇīndra," and in place of *e* and *o*, there are *ai* and *au*. It is also designated as "vṛddhi."
44. The five Pāṇḍavas, beginning with Svāda, are "Ghuṭaḥ" and "Suṭaḥ. ||44||
45. The Lord of the Vṛṣṇis [bestowed] heaven upon his friend among the Pāṇḍavas.
Ai āy (Sa.pra. 64), ... two friends, friends.
sakhāyam, sakhāyau, sakhīn || 45 ||

46. The word *sakhi* (friend), when ending in the sound *i*, is treated as if it were *hari* [with respect to case endings] except in the nominative singular and the following cases; however, in the nominative singular, it is treated as *pati* when not in a compound.
[Examples: *sakhyā*, *sakhibhyām*, *sakhibhiḥ*;
*sakhye*, *sakhibhyām*, *sakhibhyaḥ*.

47. After *sakhi* and *stri*, *us* is substituted for the endings *ṅasi* and *ṅas*. This refers to the forms *sakhi* and *strī* after the substitution of *rām* (the genitive singular ending) has been applied to the stems *ti* and *tī*. [Examples: *sakhyuḥ*, *sakhibhyām*, *sakhibhyaḥ*; *sakhyuḥ*, *sakhyoḥ*, *sakhīnām*.
48. After the words *sakhi* and *pati*, the substitution of *au* occurs for the ending *ṅi*.

Thus: *sakhyau*, *sakhyoḥ*, *sakhiṣu*; *he sakhe*, *he sakhāyau*, *he sakhāyaḥ*. Even when these endings follow a compound ending in *sakhi*, some say: *bahusakhyā*, *bahusakhye*, *bahusakhyuḥ*, *bahusakhyau*. Regarding the ablative case (*pañcamī*), the *Mahābhāṣya* and other works cite the example *susakher āgacchati* ("he comes from a good friend"). Having observed this very point, Kṛṣṇapaṇḍita states in his *Prakriyā* that "in a compound, *sakhi* is designated as *ghisamjñā*" (Pāṇini 7.3.118), noting that the mention of "compound" (*samāsa*) is merely illustrative.

Therefore, in the present context, although there is a plural suffix in the preceding [forms], [the forms] *bahusakhiḥ* and so forth follow the pattern of the word *pati*. For the word *pati*, the forms in the nominative and accusative cases follow the paradigm of *hari*; from the instrumental case onwards, they follow the paradigm of *sakhi*. However, for the compound-ending (*samāsānta*), they follow exactly the paradigm of *hari*, as in *bahupatinā*, *bahupataye*, and so forth.

The word *daityapramī* ends in the vowel *ī*. Derived from the root *mī* with the suffix *kvip*, it means "one who kills or destroys the Daityas" and thus denotes Viṣṇu. The forms are: *daityapramīḥ*, *daityapramyau*, *daityapramyaḥ*. Because this is a verbal derivative (*dhātu*), the rule regarding the substitution of *yarām* for all [consonants] in the presence of *sarveśvara* will be stated here (Viṣṇuprakāśa 50). This very example is written here for the purpose of making known the specific distinction of *vātapramī*. It should be understood in the same way elsewhere: *daityapramyam*, *daityapramyau*, *daityapramyaḥ*; *daityapramyā*, *daityapramībhyām*, *daityapramībhiḥ*.
daityapramye, daityapramībhyām, daityapramībhyaḥ;
daityapramyaḥ, daityapramībhyām, daityapramībhyaḥ;
daityapramyaḥ, daityapramyoḥ, daityapramyām.

In the case of *daityapramī*, [the forms] are *daityapramyau*, *daityapramyaḥ*, and *daityapramīṣu*; in the vocative, they are as before. Some maintain that for the word *vātapramī*, because it ends in the suffix *ī*, there is a distinction in the cases *am*, *śas*, and *ṅi*. Thus: *vātapramīm*. According to the maxim "a rule applies as long as its conditions are possible," when *trivikrama* is applied to *daśāvatāra* (Vi.Pur. 10), [the form becomes] *vātapramīn* by the rule "therefore *sa-* becomes *na-*. In the locative (*ṅi*), it is *vātapramī*. Others hold that words such as *vātapramī* and *hūhū* possess the status of verbal roots (*dhātu*). [Thus: *vātapramyam*, *vātapramīm*, *hūhvam*, *hūhūm*.
The word *viṣṇu* ends in *ur*. The derivation is accomplished by means of the *hari*-sūtras alone:
*viṣṇuḥ*, *viṣṇū*, *viṣṇavaḥ*; *viṣṇum*, *viṣṇū*, *viṣṇūn*.
viṣṇunā, viṣṇubhyām, viṣṇubhiḥ;
viṣṇave, viṣṇubhyām, viṣṇubhyaḥ;
viṣṇoḥ, viṣṇubhyām, viṣṇubhyaḥ.
viṣṇoḥ, viṣṇvoḥ, viṣṇūnām;
viṣṇau, viṣṇvoḥ, viṣṇuṣu;
he viṣṇo!

According to Amara, *cālanī* and *titaḥ* are masculine. Since this [word] is established in its base form (*prakṛti*) without sandhi within the *ūṇādi* group, there is no sandhi between the base and its case-endings. Thus, one has forms such as *titaḥ*, *titaū*, *titaavaḥ*, and so forth. ||48||

Kṛṣṇaśrī: 49. *Iy-uv-au* are substituted for *ī* and *ū* of a verbal root (*dhātu*) before the word *sarveśvara*, optionally (*bahulam*). *Īrāma* becomes *iy*, and *ūrāma* becomes *uva*. By the rule of "the beginning of a suffix," that which begins with it is included. Thus, the meaning is "before *sarveśvara*" and so forth, as well as before *viṣṇubhakta* and others. Similarly elsewhere as well. Because such a sūtra is read in the section on nouns (*nāma-prakaraṇa*), even when the *kṛt* suffix is elided, there is the status of a noun (*nāmatva*) despite the form being a verbal root. From that, the case-endings (*pratyaya*) follow: *kṛṣṇaśriyau*, *kṛṣṇaśriyaḥ*. Due to its higher priority (*paratva*), even before *am* and *śas*: *kṛṣṇaśriyam*, and so forth.

When the suffix *kvip* is applied in the sense of the abstract state (*bhāve*), we have *bhūḥ*, *bhuvaḥ*, *bhuvaḥ*. Due to the general principle of abundance, this does not apply everywhere; as it has been said: "In some cases there is application, in some cases non-application, in some cases an option, and in some cases something else entirely."
Having examined the various prescriptions of the rules in many ways, they declare that there are four types of "bāhulaka" (generalization). (This is the statement of the learned. ||49||

By that [rule]—50. For the root *sahaja-aneka-sarveśvara* ending in *kvip*, when the vowels *ī* and *ū* are not touched by contact with the true phonemes (*sat*) of the bare verbal root, they are replaced by *y* and *v*.
In that regard, in a *kṛt*-compound: *viśvanīḥ*, *viśvanyau*, *viśvanyaḥ*, and so forth. In the genitive plural: *viśvanyām*. ||47||
51. After [stems ending in] *nī* and *rā*, *ām* is substituted for the *ṅi* case-ending.

Thus: *viśvanyām*, *viśvanyoḥ*, *viśvanīṣu*. Similarly, from the irregular form *pradhīḥ* (derived from the root *dhyai* with the suffix *kvip* meaning "one who meditates intensely"): *pradhyau*. In the case of a simple *kvip*-ending stem, as in *mālīyati* ("he acts like a garland"), we have *mālīḥ*, *mālyau*; and in the *ṅi* case: *mālyi*.

What is meant by "inherently occurring" (*sahaja*)? It would not apply in the case of a subsequent conjunction (*paścādyoga*). For example: *viśvanīḥ*, *viśvanīyau*, *viśvanīyaḥ*; and in the *ām* and *ṅi* cases, *viśvaniyām*. Why "inherently occurring"? [Consider: *nīḥ*, *niyau*, *niyaḥ*. Why "not in contact with a consonant of a verbal root" (*dhātvakṣarasatsaṅgāspṛṣṭayoḥ*)? [Consider: *kṛṣṇaprīḥ*, *kṛṣṇapriyau*; *kṛṣṇapaṭaprūḥ*, *kṛṣṇapaṭapruvau*. Why "alone" (*kevala*)? In this case, it would indeed apply: *unnīḥ*, *unnyau*, *unnyaḥ*. (51)

52. For the words *sudhī* and *bhū*, [the suffixes] *iy* and *uv* are substituted respectively. By virtue of this grammatical irregularity (*nipātana*), from the root *dhyai* with the *kvip* suffix: *sudhīḥ*, *sudhiyau*, *sudhiyaḥ*. [Likewise from the root *bhū*: *kṛṣṇabhūḥ*, *kṛṣṇabhuvau*, *kṛṣṇabhuvaḥ*. ||52||

53. After *varṣābhū*, *dṛnbhū*, and *karabha*, the [substitution] of *va* occurs for *bhu*. The word *kāra* means "the act of making" (*kara*); since that too is included, both are mentioned in detail. Thus: *varṣābhūḥ*, *varṣābhvau*, *varṣābhvaḥ*; *dṛnbhūḥ*, *dṛnbhvau*. Similarly, *khalapū* and others. *kṛṣṇasukhīyati*—[the forms are] *kṛṣṇasukhīḥ*, *kṛṣṇāsukhyau*, *kṛṣṇasukhyaḥ*.

*anantīyati*—[the forms are] *anantīḥ*, *anantyau*, *anantyaḥ*. Because of the inclusion of *trivikrama* in the rule *khyatyābhyām* (Viprapañca 47), [the following forms occur] for the *ṅasi* and *ṅas* cases: *kṛṣṇasukhyuḥ*, *anantyuḥ*. Since the substitute *nara* is not treated as *sthānivat* (non-substituting) for *tarām*, [we have] *lūnyuḥ*. Some maintain that [the forms] are *kṛṣṇasukhyuḥ* and so forth. 53.
Now, those ending in the vowel ṛ. Among them is the word *pitṛ* (father). Regarding the rule beginning with *ṛrāmasakhibhyām* (Viṣṇupurāṇa-prakriyā 42):

"For the stem ending in ṛ, [the substitution of] *govinda* [occurs] before the endings of the Pāṇḍavas (i.e., the case-endings from the accusative plural onwards) and before the locative singular (*ṅau*).
Thus: *pitā*, *pitarau*, *pitaraḥ*;
pitaram, pitarau, pitṝn; pitrā, pitṛbhyām, pitṛbhiḥ;
pitre, pitṛbhyām, pitṛbhyaḥ. ||54||
55. After *ṛ* (and its substitutes), for the endings *ṅasi* and *ṅas*, there is optionally *u* in place of *as*. [Examples:
*pituḥ*, *pitṛbhyām*, *pitṛbhyaḥ*;
*pituḥ*, *pitroḥ*, *pitṝṇām*.
In the case of *pitṛ*, [the forms are] *pitari*, *pitroḥ*, and *pitṛṣu*.
56. After *buddha*, [the suffix] *govinda* is applied. 57. After *rādhā* and *viṣṇujana*, [the suffix] *īya*; after *trivikrama*, [the suffix] *sū* with the elision (*hara*) of *ra*.
O Father! Thus are the suffixes for son-in-law and so forth.
The word *nṛ* (man): *nā*, *narau*, *naraḥ*;
*naram*, *narau*, *nṝn*.
*nṛbhyaḥ*, *nṛbhyām*, *nṛbhiḥ*; however, for the word *nṛ*, [the substitution] is optional (*vi.pra. 22*)—thus *nṛṇām* or *nṝṇām*. ||5657||

The declension of the word *kartṛ* (agent): 58. Among the Pāṇḍavas, words ending in the suffixes *sṛ*, *tṛc*, and *tṛn* follow the *vṛṣṇīndra* (Kṛṣṇa) paradigm, with the exception of the vocative singular.
[Examples: *kartā*, *kartāraḥ*; *kartāram*, *kartārau*. Among the Yadus, it follows the *pitṛ* paradigm: *he kartaḥ!* (O agent!).

*Leṣṭṛ*: *leṣṭā*, *leṣṭārau*, *leṣṭāraḥ*; *leṣṭāram*, *leṣṭārau*. This [word] belongs to the *harimitra* group; the reading *hariveṇu* etc. is a corruption. Words ending in *tṛ*, *tṛṣ*, and *tṛn* are considered by the wise to belong to this class, with the exception of *pitṛ*, *mātṛ*, *bhrātṛ*, *yātṛ*, *jāmātṛ*, and *duhitṛ*. (58)

59. Regarding the word *kroṣṭṛ* when applied to the Pāṇḍavas, its form ends in the suffix *tṛc*; however, with the exception of the nominative singular (*buddha*), there is an option regarding all cases beginning with the nominative plural (*ṭādi*).
[The forms are: *kroṣṭā*, *kroṣṭārau*, *kroṣṭāraḥ*; *kroṣṭāram*, *kroṣṭārau*, *kroṣṭṝn*.

*kroṣṭrā*, *kroṣṭunā*, *kroṣṭubhyām*, *kroṣṭubhiḥ*; *kroṣṭre*, *kroṣṭave*, and so forth. That which applies whether [the suffix] has been applied or not is *nitya* (obligatory). Because the *nitya* rule is stronger, the *nuṭ* augment occurs first in place of *ām*: *kroṣṭūnām*; some say *kroṣṭr̥ṇām*. O *kroṣṭo!*; may there be prosperity for *kroṣṭrī*. (59)
The word *rai* (wealth) ends in *ā*. 60. *Rāya ā sabhoḥ*:

*kṛṣṇarāḥ*, *kṛṣṇarāyau*, *kṛṣṇarāyaḥ*; *kṛṣṇarāyam*, and so forth. The word *rai* is treated in the same way. This does not apply here: in a *taddhita* suffix, there is no substitution of *rai* [for *rājan*], as in *rai-ayati* with the *kyac* suffix. Even in Pāṇini’s grammar, this is because of the continued application of the rule *rāyo hali* [Pā. 7.2.85] and others, which follow from the context of devotion to Viṣṇu. 60.

The word *go* at the end of a compound [denotes] a bull and so forth, while in the sense of *Puruṣottama* (the Supreme Person) it possesses the characteristic marks of that;— 61. *o* and *au* [are the dual endings] among the Pāṇḍavas.
*Gauḥ*, *gāvau*, *gāvaḥ*. ||61||
62. O ā amśasoḥ na ca saḥ naḥ.
Otherwise, as in the case of *vātapramī*, the suffix *su* would not occur in the form *gāḥ*. [The forms are:
*gām*, *gāvau*, *gāḥ*; *gavā*, *gobhyām*, *gobhiḥ*.
*gave*, *gobhyām*, *gobhyaḥ*; by the rule "from *e* and *o*, [the case endings] *ṅasi* and *ṅas*" [Vi-pra. 36], etc., there is the elision of the vowel *a*:
*goḥ*, *gobhyām*, *gobhyaḥ*.

*gauḥ*, *gavoḥ*, *gavām*, and so forth. The elision (*hara*) [of the case-ending] is stronger than all other rules; and the substitution of *sarveśvara* for *hari* is stronger [than the elision], as is the rule regarding the "internal" (*antaraṅga*) and so on, by virtue of the power of the specific injunction. There is no elision of the nominative suffix (*su*) in the vocative *he gauḥ!* The word *glau* ending in *aurām* is *glauḥ*, *glāvau*, *glāvaḥ*, and so forth. ||62||
Thus end the lingas of Puruṣottama, culminating in Sarveśvara.
Now, those ending with Sarveśvara are the *lakṣmī-liṅgas*.
63. The *lakṣmī* ending with Ārāma is named Rādhā and also named Śraddhā. Therein, regarding the word "Rādhā": according to [Viṣṇupurāṇa 5.7], "from Rādhā and Viṣṇujana"—thus, Rādhā. 63.
64. From *rādhā* and *brahmā*, [the forms] *au* and *ī* [are derived].
In the non-dual (*advaya*) and dual (*dvaya*) [cases], [the forms are] *e* (according to *Saṃkṣiptasāraprakriyā* 48)—thus, *rādhe* and *rādhāḥ*. 64.
65. In the case of *rādhā*, [the forms are]: *rādhayā*, *rādhābhyām*, *rādhābhiḥ*.
66. From *rādhā*, [the forms] among the *yāp* and *ṛṣṇi* [endings are as follows]:
for the dual *ai*, [it is] *rādhāyai*; [for the dual *bhyām*,] *rādhābhyām*; [for the plural *bhyas*,] *rādhābhyaḥ*.
*rādhāyāḥ*, *rādhābhyām*, *rādhābhyaḥ*;
*rādhāyāḥ*, *rādhayoḥ*, *rādhānām*.

According to the rule *ṇer ām* (Vibhaktiprakriyā 51), because of the principle that "between a derivative form and a primitive form, the primitive alone is to be understood," the suffix *luṭ* is not included here.

*rādhāyām*, *rādhayoḥ*, *rādhāsu*. In the vocative: according to the maxim that "that which depends on fewer elements is internal (*antaraṅga*), while that which depends on more external elements is external (*bahiraṅga*)," and further, "that which depends on fewer [phonemes] is internal, while that which depends on more is external," and by the rule that "between an internal and an external operation, the internal one is stronger," first the substitution of *e* is applied; then, by the rule "there is the non-appearance of *e* and *o* when followed by *a* or *an*" (Vibhaktyadhyāya 25), we have: *he rādhe*.

In this same way, [the names] Ramā, Rāmā, Aśraddhā, Mālā, and so forth, as well as Ambā and others, are formed. Because of the inclusion of Lakṣmī [in the rule], the designation "Rādhā" is not included here. Regarding compounds, Vāmana will state [in Samāsaprakriyā 56]: "To Kṛṣṇa, who is fond of Rādhā" (*priyarādhāya kṛṣṇāya*).
67. *Vāmana* [is used] for *ambā* and others, as well as for *gopī*, when referring to the intellect (*buddhi*).
O mother! O akka! O atta! O alla! O appa! O abba! These alone are *ambā* and the rest. It is not used here in forms such as: O ambāḍe! O ambāle! O ambike! and so forth. 67.
Now, for *jarā* (old age) [in the case of the stem *jaras*]:
In the locative singular of all cases, *sarveśvare*, [the forms are] *jarā*,
*jarasau*, *jare*, and *jarasaḥ*, *jarāḥ*.
Just as the word *jarā* (old age) is analyzed as *jara-sam* [that which leads to decay], so too the word *nirjara* (immortal) is analyzed accordingly.

Words ending in *īra* denote devotion, just as the word *hari* is used for the Pāṇḍavas; thus, in the form *bhakti-śas*, it means "one who has devotion as his fruit" or "one whose self is devotion," and so forth.

69. Here, in the case of *niś* and *nāsikā*, the substitutes *niśna* and *sāva* should be stated as optional before vowel endings (*u*-class and following). Furthermore, the usage in the alternative case should be understood as being like [the forms] ending in *viṣṇujan*.

For example: *niśaḥ*, *niśāḥ*, *nijbhyām*, and so forth. The word *bhakti* ends in *īrām*. Its declension among the Pāṇḍavas is like that of the word *hari*. In the *śas* case: *bhaktīḥ*; however, because of the specific rule "in the masculine" (*vi.pra.* 10), there is no substitution of *nirām*. But because of the rule "not in the feminine" (*vi.pra.* 35), there is no substitution of *nā*. [The forms are: *bhaktyā*, *bhaktibhyām*, *bhaktibhiḥ*. ||69||
70. *harita* (green), *āpvā* (attained), *vṛṣṇiṣu* (among the bulls), *lakṣmām* (the mark)—these are always to be protected by the cowherdesses. Water caused by the bull is not sin.
[The forms] *bhaktyai*, *bhaktaye*, *bhaktibhyām*, *bhaktibhyaḥ*.
From *bhakti*: *bhaktyāḥ*, *bhakteḥ*, *bhaktibhyām*, *bhaktibhyaḥ*;
*bhaktyāḥ*, *bhakteḥ*, *bhaktyāḥ*, *bhaktīnām*.
Even within the *ā*-stem, by the rule "from two words ending in *ā*, *ṅe* becomes *ām*" (*Vipraprabodha* 51): *bhaktyām*, *bhaktau*, *bhaktyoḥ*, *bhaktiṣu*.
O devotee!
Thus [are] *buddhi*, *mati*, *bhūti*, *kṛti*, *dhṛti*, *ruci*, and so forth.
Now, as for the word *dhenu*:
Dhenuḥ, dhenū, dhenavaḥ;
dhenum, dhenū, dhenūḥ, and so forth. Among the vṛṣṇis—

*dhenvai*, *dhenave*; *dhenvāḥ*, *dhenoḥ*; *dhenvām*, *dhenau*. This same [substitution] is to be understood even in the case where *aśanī* and others possess the status of *lakṣmī*. Here, it must be stated that this applies only when *hari* is inherently *lakṣmī*. Therefore, it does not apply here: *priyaharaye*, *priyaviṣṇave*, *śriyai*. Likewise, *priyaharīḥ*. But as for the substitution of *na* (Vi.Pra. 35), it does not apply in *priyaharyā*. Some, however, say there is an option (*vikalpa*) for words such as *paṭu*: *paṭave*, *paṭvai*. ||70||
Regarding the word *tri* [meaning] *lakṣmī*:
71. For *tri* and *catur* when standing in *lakṣmī*, there are *tisṛ* and *catasṛ* [respectively] in the devotion to Viṣṇu.
72. *Tisṛ* and *catasṛ* [occur] with *raḥ* in the Lord of All.
tisraḥ, tisraḥ, tisṛbhiḥ, tisṛbhyaḥ, tisṛbhyaḥ, tisṛṇām, tisṛṣu.
The word *gopī* ends in *ī*. Here, *ī* is a suffix prescribed for *lakṣmī*—namely, *ī* and *ū* are the technical names for *lakṣmī*;
they also bear the technical name *nadī* (feminine noun).
gopī, gopyau, gopyaḥ;
gopīm, gopyau, gopīḥ;
gopyā, gopībhyām, gopībhiḥ.
gopyai, gopībhyām, gopībhyaḥ;
gopyāḥ, gopībhyām, gopībhyaḥ;
gopyāḥ, gopyoḥ, gopīnām.

*gopyām*, *gopyoḥ*, *gopīṣu*, *he gopi!*—here, by the force of the rule for *vāman* (shortening), *govindaḥ* does not apply. Similarly for *nadī*, *mahī*, and so forth. And regarding *sakhī*: *sakhī*, *sakhyau*. Here, the technical rule (*paribhāṣā*) stating that "when a word is mentioned, it includes its gender-specific forms" is not accepted. In the locative singular (*ṅau*): *sakhyām*. Thus, in *supathī*, there is no substitution of *n*. Because of the specific restriction "from Trivikrama" (*vi.pra. 57*), the elision of *su* does not occur here: *atigopiḥ*. In the masculine, among the Vṛṣṇis: *atigopaye*, etc. In the feminine, *lakṣmī*: *atigopyai*, *atigopaye*, etc.
In words such as *avītantrī*, *tarīlakṣmī*, *īdhīṇī*,
and *ṇāmuṇādi*, the elision of the suffix *su* never occurs.

*Lakṣmīḥ*, *lakṣmyau*, *lakṣyaḥ*, and so forth, follow the pattern of *gopī*. However, the word *tantrī* (meaning "lute string") is established by adding the suffix *īp* to the root *tantr* ending in the suffix *aṇ*. ||73||
Because it belongs to the *gaurādi* group, the word *strī* ends in long *ī*. From that, the nominative suffix *su* is elided.

74. In the presence of *sarveśvara*, *iy* and *uv* replace [the final vowel and penultimate consonant] of *strī* and *bhrū*; [and] for *strī*, [these replacements] optionally occur before the case-endings *am* and *śas*.
Thus: *strī*, *striyau*, *striyaḥ*.
striyam, striyam; striyau;
striyaḥ, strīḥ | striyā, strībhyām, strībhiḥ | "Always feminine" (Viśvapradīpa 70).
striyai, strībhyām, strībhyaḥ;
striyāḥ, strībhyām, strībhyaḥ;
striyāḥ, striyoḥ, strīṇām—as in "Viṣṇu is stronger than Viriñci."

In the feminine: *striyām*, *striyoḥ*, *strīṣu*; *he stri*. However, when [the word] is secondary (*gauṇatva*) and masculine, it is *atistriḥ*. But because of the rule "sometimes" (*kvacit*), there may be an application of the *tadantavidhi* (extension of a grammatical operation to that which ends with the specified term). In this regard, because of the mention of "sometimes" (*kvacid*) in the *Vipraprabodha* (67), the detailed explanation is that the substitution of *iy* occurs in the feminine for [words ending in] *go* and *vindu*, with the exception of *anuḍuh*. Furthermore, there is another opinion: that this is not the view of Bhartṛhari and others.
*atistriyau*, *atistriyaḥ*;
*atistriyam*, *atistriyau*, *atistriyaḥ*; *atistrīn*; *atistriṇā*.
atistriye, atistreḥ, atistriyoḥ, atistrīṇām, atistrau

In the sense of "excellent woman" (lakṣmyām śastāparatve): *atistriyaḥ*, *atistrīḥ*, *atistriyā*. In the sense of "among the Vṛṣṇis" (*vṛṣṇiṣu pakṣe*): *atistriyai*, *atistraye*, *atistriyāḥ*, *atistriyām*. ||74||
Regarding the word *śrī*: by the rule *śriyau*, *śriyaḥ*, etc., [it is derived from] the root *śrī* according to *śrī-dhātor īd-ūt-au* (Viprapannaprakāśa 49).
75. The station of the arrows is the *gopī*; without a woman, [it is] among the Vṛṣṇis or [in] me.

*Śriyai*, *śriye*, *śrībhyām*, *śrībhyaḥ*; *śriyāḥ*, *śriyaḥ*; *śriyāḥ*, *śriyaḥ*, *śriyoḥ*; *śrīṇām*, *śriyām*; *śriyām*, *śriyi*, *śriyoḥ*, *śrīṣu*; *he śrīḥ*. In this same way are *dhī* and the others, as well as *bhrū* and the others. *bhrūḥ*, *bhruvau*, *bhruvaḥ*; likewise *subhrūḥ*. According to some, [the forms] *buddhe*, *vāmane* [are used]. Thus it is said: "‘Āḥ! Alas, what misery! Oh, how strange! Hūṃ! O Mother, the deities! Fie! Alas, Father, where are you? O fair-browed one! In this manner he lamented excessively. [Bhaṭṭikāvya 6.11] Thus it ends.

In connection with the word *pra*, *pradhīḥ* (an excellent intellect) is formed as follows: nominative singular *pradhīḥ*, dual *pradhiyau*, plural *pradhiyaḥ*; dative singular *pradhiyai* or *pradhiye*. Regarding this, there is a misconception concerning the substitution of *yā*; for according to that [misconceived] view, there is an absence of the status of being preceded by a *gati* or a *kāraka*. Indeed, the designation *gati* applies to prefixes like *pra-* only when they are connected with a verb (*kriyā*). To say that it applies even when preceded by a mere indeclinable (*avyaya*) is un-Pāṇinian. As for the word *punarbhū* signifying a remarried woman, which is always feminine: in the vocative singular, *he punarbhu*, even when it occurs as a separate word (*bhinnapada*), the substitution of *ṇ* for *n* should be stated.
Now for words beginning with *vadhū*: like the word *lakṣmī*—*vadhūḥ*, *vadhvau*, *vadhvaḥ*; *he vadhu!* (O bride!).

Furthermore, they say that even though *aniṣū* is masculine, it retains the designation *gopī*; therefore, the word *bahupreyasī*—like the word *gopī*—is used in the masculine even without the suffix *śas*. Similarly, *atilakṣmīḥ* is like the word *lakṣmī*. The *Bhāṣya* states that this is established because [the suffix] refers to a feminine constituent part (*avayava*). However, the author of the *Prakriyā* says it is like *vātapramī*, which ends in the suffix *ī*. As for the form *bahupreyasīḥ*, the nominative plural suffix *su* is elided due to its being secondary (*gauṇa*). Moreover, the designation *gopī* does not apply to the Vṛṣṇis; such is the detailed explanation. This, however, is un-Pāṇinian.

Likewise, from the form *gopīm icchati* (desiring a cowherd-maid), after the addition of the suffix *kyac*, the suffix *kvip* is applied, resulting in *gopī* = Kṛṣṇa. In the singular (*sau*), it is like *gopīvān*. In the plural ending in *śas*, it is again like a verbal root, thus *gopīvataḥ*. However, they do not accept the designation *gopī* when the suffix *vānamat* is present. As for the commentary stating "of one who has surpassed a female friend" (*atisakheḥ*), this refers to *anisuvām* [Viprapañca 75]. Why [is the example] *atiśriye gopīsaṅghāya*? Some, however, desire the suffix *āp* here. When *ī* and *ū* are not inherently Lakṣmī, the designation *gopī* does not apply; thus, it is not *śriyai*.

The word *mātṛ* is like *pitṛ*: *mātā*, *mātārau*, *mātaraḥ*; but in the *śas* [nominative plural], it is *mātṛḥ*. The word *svasṛ* is like *kartṛ*: *śvasā*, *śvasārau*, *śvasāraḥ*; but in the *śas*, it is *svasaḥ*. Regarding the word *rai*, Kṣīrasvāmī says that some hold it to be feminine (*strī*); therefore, it follows the previous pattern. The word *go* is as before. The word *dyo* is like *go*, and the word *nau* is like *glau*. ||75||
Thus end the marks of Lakṣmī culminating in Sarveśvara.
Now, those ending with Sarveśvara are Brahma-liṅgas;
therein, the word Gokula ends with Arāma—76. [The sequence] from Brahma to Kṛṣṇa is Sora.
The *daśāvatārādaṃ śasorarāmaharaḥ* (Vi.Pra. 9) is Gokula; the *rādhābrahmabhyāmau ī* (Vi.Pra. 64) is also Gokula. ||76||

77. *Brahmata* [is substituted] for *jas* and *śas*; *śi*. Since [the substitute] consists of a single phoneme (*ekavarṇatva*), it would follow that it applies only at the end; however, by the rule "A *śit* [substitute] replaces the whole," a *śit* substitute applies to the entire [original form]. ||77||
78. At the end of the words *sarveśvara* and *vaiṣṇava*, there is *nuṃ* [nasalization]; at the end of *umā*, there is *vit* [the doubling of the following consonant]. ||78||
79. The position following the final *sarveśvara* is called *mita*. 80.
The vowel preceding the final [consonant] is designated as *uddhava*; the ancients call it *upadhā*. 80.
81. *abrahman*, *pāṇḍava*, *śiśu*, and *kṛṣṇa* are designated as *sthāna*. Some say they are designated as *ghuṭ*; others say they are designated as *sarvanāman*. ||81||

82. *Nāntadhātu-varjita-sānta-sat-saṅga-mahad-apām uddhavasya trivikramaḥ kṛṣṇasthāne, vinā buddham*. The analysis is as follows: *nāntasya* (ending in *n*), *dhātu-varjita* (excluding verbal roots), *sānta* (ending in *s*), *sat* (existing), *saṅga* (association), *mahataḥ* (of the word *mahat*), and *apaḥ* (the word *ap*)—this is the division [of the compound]. Thus, *gokulāni* [is formed]. This applies likewise in the second case. In the third case and onwards, it is like *puruṣottama*. Because it occupies the position of *buddha*, this [word *go*] is also designated as *buddha*—O *gokula*! Similarly, [the rules apply to] *kula*, *phala*, *mūla*, and so forth. 82.

83. For *hṛdaya*, [the forms] *hṛdi* or *hṛtsu* [are used]; or, according to some, *śīrṣasya* or *śīrṣan*. The applications in the alternative case should be understood as being like those for words ending in *-jan* or *-vat*. For example: *hṛndi* or *hṛdayāni*; *hṛdā* or *hṛdayena*. In both cases, [the plural forms] are *śīrṣāṇi*. Regarding *jarā*, [the form] *jaras* occurs before all case-endings (*sarveśvara*) [according to Viśvarūpa’s Prauḍhamanoramā 68]: *nirjaram* or *nirjarasam*; *nirjare* or *nirjarasī*. They maintain that the substitution of *jaras* occurs prior to the *num* augment.
84. For the *na* and *ma* that do not end in *viṣṇupada*, there is indeed the *viṣṇucakra* [mark] in the case of a Vaiṣṇava.
*Nirjarāṇi* and *nirjarāṃsi*; again, likewise. In the case of *buddhe*: "O *nirjara*! and "O *nirjarasaṃ*!"—so say some. 84.
The word *dadhi* ends in *irām*. 85. From *brahma*, there is the great extraction of its own vowel: *dadhi*. How [is it] *gokulam*? Because it is not formed therein. 85.
86. From *brahma* up to *īśān* [the vowels] are followed by *nu*; in *sarveśvara*, however, it is not *ām*.
In the case of *uk*, there is elision (*it*). [Examples: *dadhinī*, *dadhīni*. Again, it is like that. 86.

87. For the words *dadhi*, *asthi*, *sakthi*, and *akṣi*, [the substitution of] *irām* occurs before the suffix *an* when followed by *sarveśvara*. 88. That which is not *kṛṣṇa*, nor situated in a [specific] place, is designated as *bhagavat*; and when a *taddhita* suffix follows, it is also [so designated].
Here, according to the followers of Pāṇini (*yaci bham*, 1.4.18), the base form receives the designation *bha*. ||88||

89. For the word *dadhi*, which is devoid of the suffixes *bha* and *satsaṅga*, the [substitution] *an* replaces the final vowel and the following consonant (*arāma*) before the vocative singular ending, but not before those [other case endings]; however, for the two [vowels *i* and *ī*], the substitution *vā* (or *at*) applies.
Thus: *dadhnā*, *dadhibhyām*, *dadhibhiḥ*; *dadhne*, *dadhibhyām*, *dadhibhyaḥ*, and so forth.
ṅau—dadhni, dadhani ||89||

90. [The substitution of *i* for *an* occurs] after *brahman*, *govinda*, and *buddha*. Examples: *he dadhe!* (O curd!); *he dadhi!* (O curd!). Likewise for *asthi*, *sakthi*, and *akṣi*. When it has surpassed the curd (*dadhi*), as in *atidadhnā* by a cowherd (*gopāla*) or a cowherdess (*gopālī*). By its very nature, the word *dadhi* is understood here as *brahman* itself. Thus, "it holds" (*dadhati*) is *dadhi*; by that, *tena dadhinā*. Why [is the rule qualified] by "of this [word]" (*irāmasya*)? [To exclude cases like] *padmākṣeṇa* (by one with lotus-eyes). Examples: *vāri*, *vāriṇī*, *vārīṇi*.
vāri, vāriṇī, vārīṇi;
vāriṇā, vāribhyām, vāribhiḥ; vāriṇe, and so forth; [genitive plural] vārīṇām.
madhu, madhunī, madhūni ||90||

91. After *brahman* and *trivikrama*, the substitution of *vāmana* occurs [for the final vowel and the preceding consonant]. Thus, we have *viśvani*, *vaśvaninī*, and *viśvanīni*. However, in cases such as *gokulābhyām*, the substitution of *vāmana* does not occur; this is because the rule for *trivikrama* depends on both [the preceding and following elements] and is therefore considered *bahiraṅga* (external). This follows the principle to be stated later: "When an internal operation (*antaraṅga*) is being performed, that which is established by an external factor (*bahiraṅga*) should not serve as its cause," or simply because it is not applied in those instances. 91.

92. Regarding the suffix *ṭā* and others in the sense of "belonging to the same object" (*samānārthatā*), it is applicable to the Supreme Person (*puruṣottama*) and the Lord (*īśa*), as in *brahmapuruṣottama*; or to the Lord of all (*sarveśvara*). Examples: *viśvanya*, *viśvaninā*. In the *āmi* [case], examples are *viśvanyām*, *viśvanīnām*. Here, the quality of being the impeller of the universe is common to both the Supreme Person and Brahman. However, when the meaning is not the same—as in the case of the masculine *pīlu* (a tree)—it is not so for Brahman or its fruit, but only for the *pīlu* tree itself. In the former case, the meaning is "being that tree," while in the latter, it is "produced from that"; thus there is a difference in meaning. ||92||

In the word *kṛṣṇarai*, [the vowel] *irāma* alone [is substituted]; for—93. In place of *ea*, *irāma* is substituted; in place of *oa*, *urāma* would be the substitute. Thus: *kṛṣṇari*, *kṛṣṇariṇī*, *kṛṣṇarīṇi*.

*kṛṣṇarāyā*, *kṛṣṇaribhiḥ*. According to the principle that "a modification affecting one part does not alter the identity of the whole"—*kṛṣṇarābhyām*, *kṛṣṇarāyām*. Except for *sabhoḥ* (*vi.pra.* 60), there is no substitution of *ā*—*kṛṣṇarīṇām*. Regarding the suffix *ṭāmoḥ*: *kṛṣṇarāṇā* and *kṛṣṇarāṇām*—this alone is the opinion of Jumara. However, regarding the suffix *āmi*, *kṛṣṇarāṇām* alone is the opinion of Ujjvaladatta. For those [grammarians] who maintain that the substitution of *ā* occurs even in the mere sense of devotion to Viṣṇu (as in *viṣṇujanādi*), the author of the *Prakriyā* has not accepted their view that the substitution of *nā* would also apply on the grounds of the "condition of immediate sequence" (*sannipātalakṣaṇa*). This principle of *sannipātalakṣaṇa* will be explained later (*ā.pra.* 187).

Of the word *sudyu*: *sudyu*, *sudyunī*, *sudūni*. In the case of [suffixes] beginning with *ṭ*—*sudyuvā*, *sudyunā*. O *sudyo*! O *sudyu*! *Cartṛ* (agent): due to the strength of the Brahma-rule (*brahmakārya*) regarding the separate classification, [the forms are] not like *vṛṣṇīndra*—namely, *kartṛṇi*, *kartṛṇi*. In the case of [suffixes] beginning with *ṭ*—*kartrā*, *kartṛṇā*. O *kartaḥ*! O *kartṛ*!

Likewise, *priyakroṣṭunī*, *priyakroṣṭūni*. Here too, there is the delusion that the substitution of *tṛ* occurs; however, the *Kāśikā* states that before the substitution of *tṛ*, *num* and *nuṭ* occur by way of a counter-exception (*vipratiṣedha*). The *Padacandrikā* says that the state of being *kroṣṭu* is superseded by *num* because it is subsequent. And the *Kātantra* and its commentary (*Vistara*) maintain that a rule concerning an augment (*āgama*) is stronger [than a rule concerning a substitute].

*Tatpriyatri* refers to that *gokula* (cow-pen) in which three beloveds reside. Even though there is a great reduction [of the stem], the state of being "three" (*tisṛ*) is seen in forms such as *kāśikā*, etc., as in *priyatisṛ*. If this is so, then the counter-example for the rule regarding devotion to Viṣṇu (*viṣṇubhakti*) should be understood as *tritva* (the state of being three) in the context of secondary derivatives (*taddhita*), etc. Thus: *priyatisṛṇī*, *priyatisṛṇi*, *priyatisrā*, *priyatisṛṇā*. In the cases of the *ṅasi* and *ṅas* endings: *priyatisraḥ*, because the application of the *ra* substitute is obligatory. Likewise, *priyacatasṛ*. However, the author of the *Vistarakāra* allows an option; by his view, *priyatri* and *priyacatuḥ* are also valid.

The words *sānu* and others possess both genders inherently: *sānunā*, *sānave*. According to Amarasimha, "A ridge (*snu*), a plateau (*prastha*), and a slope (*sānu*) are not feminine. Following the word *madhu*, the grammatical derivation (*prakriyā*) stating "in this way, *ambu*, *sānu*, and so forth" [Pāṇini 7.1.75] is to be considered doubtful. 93.
Thus end the Brahma-lingas, culminating in Sarveśvara.

Now, words ending in *viṣṇujan* (e.g., *puruṣottama*) have masculine gender (*puṃliṅga*), while certain words ending in *carām* (e.g., *pratyak*) have common gender (*vācyaliṅga*). Regarding the latter: from the root *añc* preceded by *prati*, the suffix *kvip* is applied. There is elision of *kvip* and elision of the nasal *n*. Then, the substitution of *ṣ* occurs. From that word *pratyak*, the case-endings (*svādayaḥ*) are added. 94. For vowels (*ac*) and for those [consonants] having *c*, *t*, *m*, or *ṇ* as their indicatory marks (*anubandha*), the augment *nuṃ* is inserted in place of *kṛṣṇa* (i.e., before the vowel).
In the phrase "rādhāviṣṇujanābhyām" (Viṣṇupurāṇa 5.7), the case-ending *su* is elided. ||94||
95. When there is a conjunction with the *ca*-group (*cavarga*), the *ta*-group (*tavarga*) becomes the *ca*-group.
96. At the end of a word following *sat-saṅga*, there is elision (*hara*) when followed by the word *viṣṇu*.
97. At the end of the word *viṣṇu*, the *ca*-group becomes the *ka*-group; however, in the case of a Vaiṣṇava [mantra], it becomes the *sa*-group.
Facing westward.
98. There is optionally doubling of a consonant belonging to Viṣṇu (a non-nasal stop) before a pause.

A "pause" (virāma) is the non-appearance of a following letter. However, in the case of the *savarga* (homogeneous group of stops), as in *pratyaṅ* + *añca*, we have *pratyaṅ-añcau* and *pratyaṅ-añcaḥ*; *pratyañcam*, *pratyañcau*. Why [is there no doubling] in *tac-śaureḥ* or *bhagavān-c-śūraḥ*? Because [the rule] was not formulated for those cases.

99. In the case of the word *bhagavati*, the vowel *a* is replaced by *i*, and the preceding [vowel] is replaced by *e* (trivikrama). According to the maxim that "when the cause (*nimitta*) is removed, the effect (*naimittika*) is also removed," the *yarāma* is replaced by *irāma*. Thereafter, the *trivikrama* occurs: *pratīcaḥ*, *pratīcā*.

100. Regarding the status of the preceding [element] as being like *viṣṇupada* in the case of *svādi-taddhita* suffixes such as *ayasa*, *sarva*, *īśvara*, and so on, [the rule] beginning with "pratyabhyām" and so forth applies. In the rule "cavargasya" (Viṣṇupurāṇa-prakriyā 97), the mention of *vaiṣṇava* indicates that the meaning of the verbal root alone is intended, serving as a signifier (*jñāpaka*) that the application of other rules extends up to that point. Thus, according to the Easterners (*prācya*). Likewise, for *pitracitya* in the *śas* [case], [the form is] *pitṛcaḥ*. The claim that "only for *ananta* there is *trivikrama*" is an error regarding that [rule], because the governing authority (*adhikāra*) of that [term] has ceased. For *tiryac*: *tiryaṅ*, *tiryañcau*, *tiryañcaḥ*; *tiryañcam*, *tiryañcau*.
101. *Tiryak* means "horizontal"; *tiraścī* and *udīcī* mean "northward" in the sense of "O Blessed One"; *irāmaita* means "go horizontally. *Tiraścaḥ*.
tiraścā, tiryagbhyām, tiryagbhiḥ. Likewise for udac— udaṅ, udañcam, udañcau, udīcaḥ.
*udīcā*, *udagbhyām*, and so forth.
*kruñ*— *kruṅ*, *kruñcau*, *kruñcaḥ*.
kruñcam, kruñcau, kruñcaḥ;
kruñcā, kruṅbhyām, krūṅṣu.
In this way, *añcu* is used in the sense of worship; [the forms] *pratyañcaḥ* and *prāñcaḥ* [are derived from it]. ||101||

The verbal root *vraśc* (meaning "to cut") has its *v* situated between two dentals (*da*). According to rule 102, "when *s* is followed by *ś* in conjunction with a *ca*-class consonant," the form *vraśc* remains. Then, when the suffix *kvip* is elided following the word *daitya*, the *r* of *rarāma* becomes *ṛrāma*. Thus, we have *daityavṛśc*; the case-ending *su* is then dropped. ||102||

103. In the case of the roots *chaś*, *rāj*, *bhrāj*, *parivrāj*, *sṛj*, *mṛj*, *bhrasj*, and *vraśc*, the letter *y* occurs at the end of a *viṣṇupada* (a word ending in *visarjanīya*) and before a *vaiṣṇava* (a following vowel).
Furthermore, when the occasional (*naimittika*) cause [the *visarjanīya*] has ceased, it remains as the dental [letter *j*] in the middle.

104. When *skoḥ* (the consonants *s* and *k*) are followed by *sat-saṅga* and the like, there is elision (*hara*) of the *y*, provided it is at the end of a *viṣṇupada* or before a *vaiṣṇava* [vowel].
105. When *ṣa* is followed by *ḍa*, there is elision of the *y*, provided it is at the end of a *viṣṇupada* or before *hari-ghoṣa*.
106. For *viṣṇudāsa*, *harikamala* may optionally be substituted at the pause (*virāma*).
*daityavṛṭ*, *daityavṛḍ*, *daityavṛścau*, *daityavṛścaḥ*;
*daityavṛḍbhyām*; *daityavṛṭsu*.

Regarding *jalamuc*: although the elision of the *s* is established by the rule "only through association with the good is Hari [attained]" (*satsaṅgāntahareṇaiva*), the inclusion of the term *viṣṇujana* in the rule *rādhāviṣṇujanābhyām* (ViP 57) implies that the elision does not apply here by the rule *skoḥ* (ViP 104).
jalamuk, jalamug, jalamucau, jalamucaḥ, jalamugbhyām ||106||

107. In the case of words such as *ac* that denote the *pratyāhāras* of Pāṇini, as well as in the case of the imitation (*anukaraṇa*) of *uṅ*, *nañ*, and *añ*, the *ka*-class [consonants] and so forth do not occur. For example:
*ac*, *acaḥ*, *acaḥ*; *ajbhyām*. According to the rule *sasya śaḥ* (Viṣamapadaprakāśa 102), in *acśu*, when *cha* is substituted, it becomes *acchu*. Similarly: *uṅ*, *uñau*, *uñaḥ*.

*yadurāj*—*yadurāṭ*, *yadurāḍ*, *yadurājau*, *yadurājaḥ*. From the root *bhrasj* with the suffix *kvip*, [by the rule] "the elision of that which ends in *sat-saṅga*" (*vi.pra.* 96), we have *bhṛṭ*, *bhṛḍ*, *bhṛjjau*, *bhṛjjaḥ*. ||107||
108. In the case of *sraj*, *diś*, *dṛś*, *ṛtvij*, *juṣṇiṣ*, *dadhr̥ṣ*, *nudaka*, and those preceded by *spṛś*, *tādṛś*, etc., [the suffix] *k* occurs at the end of the word.
One who sacrifices at the proper season (*ṛtu*) is an *ṛtvij*; [the forms are] *ṛtvij*, *ṛtvijau*.

Regarding the masculine noun *yuj* (meaning "yoked"): 109. The augment *num* is applied in place of *kṛṣṇa* [i.e., before the suffixes beginning with *ka*] when the word is not part of a compound, but not when it has the sense of "concentration" (*samādhi*).

Here, there is a misconception regarding the rule for *suṭ*. The forms are: *yuṅ*, *yuñjau*, *yuñjaḥ*; *yugbhyām*. When it is part of a compound or has the meaning of "concentration," there is no *num*. Examples: *kṛṣṇayuk*, *kṛṣṇayug*, *kṛṣṇayujau*, *kṛṣṇayujaḥ*; *kṛṣṇayugbhyām*. In the sense of "concentration": *yuk*, *yujau*. 109.

*Ūrjaḥ* in the masculine—110. *Rāt sasyaiva sat-saṅgānaharavidhiḥ*. This is a restrictive rule (*niyama*): a restriction is a limitation when there is a possibility of multiple applications. *Ūrk*, *ūrj*, *ūrjau*, *ūrjaḥ*. *Viśvasṛj*: *viśvasṛṭ*, *viśvasṛḍ*; *viśvasṛjau*, *viśvasṛjaḥ*. According to some, "when *tvaṃ* does not follow"—*viśvasṛk*, *viśvasṛṭsu*.

Regarding that, Trivikrama states: "In the masculine, [the suffix *num* is applied] after a stem ending in *n*, excluding verbal roots" (*vi.pra.* 82). Here, because [the rule for *num*] is not formulated, and because of the aforementioned principle—"sometimes, even when an internal [operation]..."—and because of the indicator in the rule "after [stems] ending in *brahma* or *īśa*, [the suffix] *nuK*" (*vi.pra.* 86), which was taught by Sarveśvara, there is a certainty that the elision of *rāma* does not occur in a name; therefore, the elision of *su* would not occur. [Response: This is not so. The elision of *su* occurs. The elision of the final part [of the compound] following *satsaṅga* occurs. Here, because [the rule for *num*] is not formulated, and because of the aforementioned principle—"sometimes, even when an internal [operation]..."—and because of the indicator in the rule "after [stems] ending in *brahma* or *īśa*, [the suffix] *nuK*" (*vi.pra.* 86), which was taught by Sarveśvara, there is a certainty that the elision of *rāma* does not occur in a name; therefore, the elision of *su* would not occur. [Response: This is not so. The elision of *su* occurs. The elision of the final part [of the compound] following *satsaṅga* occurs.
