[Response: This is not so. The elision of *su* occurs. The elision of the final part [of the compound] following *satsaṅga* occurs. Here, because [the rule for *num*] is not formulated
mahān, mahāntau, mahāntaḥ;
mahāntam, mahāntau, mahataḥ; mahatā, mahadbhyām.
O Great One! ||110||

Bhagavat-u— 111. [The forms] of *atvasantoddhava* (the substitution of *u* for the final vowel of the stem) are *trivikramaḥ*, *buddha-varjitau*, and *sau*; [these occur] without the case-ending (*dhātuṃ*).
Bhagavān, bhagavantau, bhagavantaḥ.
bhagavantam, bhagavantau, bhagavataḥ;
bhagavatā, bhagavadbhyām. ||111||

112. *Bhagavat*, *aghavat*, *bhavat*, *tūtum*, *bhagos*, *aghos*, and *bhos* are particles used for addressing a Buddha. These are particles (*nipāta*) formed by the simultaneous substitution [of the final vowel and consonant] of both the preceding and following words. Examples: *he bhagoḥ!* (O Blessed One!), *he bhagavan!*; *he aghoḥ!* (O Sinless One!), *he aghavan!*; *he bhoḥ!* (O Sir!), *he bhavan!*; and *kathaṃ bhoḥ vaiṣṇavāḥ!* (How so, O Vaiṣṇavas?). Because they are indeclinables (*avyaya*), [the forms remain as shown]. From the word *bhagavat*: when derived from the root *bhagavat* with the suffix *ky-aṅ* (meaning "acting like one who possesses fortune") and subsequently the *kvip* suffix, we have *bhagavata*. From that, in the beginning of the nominal cases (*svādi*), the form would be exactly as in the base form, because in the state of being a noun (*nāmāvasthāyām*), it has the marker *catur-bhuja-anubandha* (indicating it is a noun). Thus: *bhagavān*.

Regarding words such as *dadat*, *jakṣat*, and others, the prohibition of the *num* augment will be stated in the section on *kṛt*-suffixes (sūtra 16): *dadat*, *dadatau*, *dadataḥ*; *dadadbhyām*. *Jakṣat*, *jakṣatau*, *jakṣataḥ*; *jakṣadbhyām*.
With the marker *ṛ* as an indicatory letter (*anubandha*): *bhavatṛ*; in the masculine: *bhavan*, *bhavantau*, *bhavantaḥ*, *bhavadbhyām*; O *bhavan*!
[The word] *muramath* [is derived from] "he crushes Mura": *muramath*, *muramathau*.
One who knows Kṛṣṇa is *kṛṣṇavit*. In the masculine: *kṛṣṇavit*, *kṛṣṇavid*, *kṛṣṇavidau*. ||112||
Regarding the word *supāt*: *supāt* [is derived] from *supāda*.
113. The word *pāt* [is used] for the Blessed One Vāmana.

*Supadaḥ*: likewise, when *pada* is substituted for the word *pād*, one has *padaḥ* and so forth. Regarding the suffix *ām*, the augment *nuṭ* is set aside, and only *viriñci-* applies. This is according to the principle that "Viṣṇu is stronger than Viriñci [Brahmā], and every Viriñci is stronger than Viṣṇu"—thus, *padām*. Vardhamāna states that in the case of *niśā*, *hṛdaya*, *māsa*, *yuṣad*, and *uṣas*, there is no *viriñci* substitution before the word *viṣṇujan* (the suffix *ām*), because it is not recorded in the *Bhāṣya*, the *Cāndra*, and other such works. However, if *viriñci* were present, then just as *ṣa* becomes *ḍa*, one should consider that *śa* becomes *ja*; furthermore, rules such as *cha-śo rāj* apply only to verbal roots (*dhātu*). From this, with the suffixes *nij* and *nic*, we have *nicśu* and *nicchu*. (113)

Regarding the root *budh* preceded by *kṛṣṇa*: from the form *kṛṣṇaṃ budhyati*, with the suffix *kvip*, we have *kṛṣṇabudh*. In the masculine: 114. For a root belonging to the *ekasarveśvara* class that begins with a consonant other than *ja* (*javarj*) and ends in *ghoṣa* (a voiced consonant), the quality of being *ghoṣavat* applies at the beginning [of the suffixes], and likewise for the suffixes *sad* and *dhv*. Thus: *kṛṣṇabhut*, *kṛṣṇabhud*, *kṛṣṇabudhau*, *kṛṣṇabudhaḥ*. Similarly, there are forms such as *tattadbhud* and others. Why "other than *ja*" (*javarji*)? Consider *jabh*—*jab*, *jabhau*, *jabhaḥ*, and so on. Why "belonging to the *ekasarveśvara* class"? Consider the root *dāmarudh* ending in *kyan* and *kvip*—*dāmarut*.

By the term *dhātu* (root), even a derivative of a root is included. Therefore, from *govinda-bhāti*, with the suffix *kap*, we have *govindabhaḥ*; then, with the suffixes *ṇi* and *kvip*, we have *govindhab*, *govindhap*, *govindabhau*, and *govindabhaḥ*. Similarly, *puṇḍrabh*, *puṇḍrapa*. Here, the *Prakriyākalāpa*, *Kāśikā*, and *Bhāṣāvṛtti* should be consulted; however, in the *Prakriyā*, *adhok* and *govindhap* would be points of inquiry. In the *Kālāpa*, they are *dāmarut* and *jap*; in the *Kāśikā* and other works, there is no doubt [regarding their forms]. (114)
O King, by the rule *nānta* (Viśvapradīpa 82), *trivikrama* [is formed]; here, the *s* is elided. 115. The *n* at the end of a name is elided when followed by the word *viṣṇu*, except after *buddha*.
There is no elision of the *n* initially, because otherwise the elision of *n* to be prescribed later in rules such as *pathin-mathin* (Viśvapradīpa 118) would be rendered purposeless.
*rājā*, *rājānau*, *rājānaḥ*;

*rājānam*, *rājānau*. By the rule "of that which is devoid of the company of *sat*" (*vi.pra.* 89), there is the removal of *ra*. By the rule "the *ca*-class [replaces] the *ta*-class" (*vi.pra.* 95), and by "in the company of *sat*, *ja* and *ña* become *jña*" (*vi.pra.* 95)—*rājñaḥ*, *rājñā*.

The meaning is that, according to the maxim— "When an internal operation is being performed, that which is external and not caused by it shall be considered as non-existent"— the substitution of *na* for *ha* would be non-existent (*asiddha*), and thus forms such as *kṛṣṇasya*, *trivikramo gopāle* (Viṣṇu Purāṇa 13), and so forth, would not be obtained. However, the designation *kṛṣṇa* should not be stated for *na* and *va* when *ha* follows—
as in *rājabhyām*, *rājabhiḥ*, *rājñe*, *rājabhyām*, *rājabhyaḥ*.
rājñaḥ, rājabhyām, rājabhyaḥ; rājñaḥ, rājñoḥ, rājñām; rājñi, rājñoḥ, rājasu.

O King! Regarding the word *yuṣmad*—in the rule "or among the Yadus" (*vi.pra.* 28) and others, there is the substitution of *yuṣan*. The meaning is that the status of being a substitute (*sthānivadbhāva*) applies only in certain cases: namely, everywhere for the substitutes of nominal stems, verbal roots, and suffixes, as well as for the substitutes of the word *viṣṇu*; however, the status of being the same individual instance (*tadvyaktivadbhāva*) applies only where it is intended for phonemes (*varṇa*). By this [principle], when it possesses the status of a nominal stem, the elision of *an* by "arāmaharaḥ" (*vi.pra.* 89) occurs: *yuṣṇaḥ*, *yuṣṇā*.

Thus, when performing the sacrifice (*yajana*), [the forms] *ātman*, *sudharmanitya*, and so forth [are derived]. However, because of the qualifying attribute "one who is devoid of the company of the wicked" (*asatsaṅgahīna*) [in Viṣṇupurāṇa 89], there is no elision of the vowel—[resulting in] *yajanaḥ* and *yajanā*. Likewise, *śvan*, *yuvan*, and *maghavan*. [The nominative plural forms are] *śvā*, *śvānau*, *śvānaḥ*. ||115||

In certain cases there is a specific rule: 116. In the case of *śvan*, *yuvan*, and *maghavan*, the substitution of *vas* for the final syllable occurs before a *bhaga-vat* (i.e., a suffix beginning with *bha*) that is not followed by *ī*. However, this does not apply when a *taddhita* suffix beginning with *ī* follows, nor in the case of *yuvatī* and similar forms. The term *vasya* is a reference to the form ending in *vas*. Examples: *Śvan*: *śunaḥ*, *śunā*, *śvabhyām*, *śvabhiḥ*. In the *śas* [locative plural] case: *yūnaḥ*, *yūnā*, *yuvabhyām*, *yuvabhiḥ*. Similarly: *maghonaḥ*, *maghonā*. Regarding the nominative singular (*sau*), the Kālāpas state: "In the nominative singular, it is either *maghavan* or *maghavā*" (Śabdaprakaraṇa, 165).
"The wind blows at its own will, the sun rises, Hari eats without fear, and that Maghavan [Indra] presides over the sacrifices"—thus says Bhaṭṭi (18.19).

There is also the word *maghavat*; it is the cause of Indra's shame regarding his thunderbolt (*vajra*). Having spoken thus, he applied it to himself, as seen in the usage: *maghavān*, *maghavantau*, *maghavantaḥ*, *maghavadbhyām*.
Now, the word *pratidivan* signifies "day": *pratidivā*, *pratidivānau*, *pratidivānaḥ*, *pratidivānam*, *pratidivānau*. (116)

117. After a root (*dhātu*) ending in *r*, *av*, *i*, or *u*, [the suffix] *trivikrama* is applied; after a root ending in *rav*, it is applied when referring to Viṣṇu’s attendants (*viṣṇujana*), but not after roots beginning with *ku* or *chur*, nor in the case of secondary suffixes (*taddhita*).

A root that has become a name is called a "name-root" (*nāmadhātu*); this will be stated [later] as "vibhuḥ" (Ā.pra. 509–563). Here, because of the specific mention [of the condition], only the phoneme *viṣṇujana* is taken, and not merely the sounds *sva* and so on. Because of the prohibition regarding *ku* and others, it should be understood that [the rule applies] elsewhere than just to a name. From that [root], in the *śas* [case]: *pratidīvnaḥ*, *pratidīvnā*.

Considering that *arāma-hara* is the cause [of the substitution], the rule for *trivikrama* is applied here; therefore, there is no status of being "not yet established" (*asiddhatva*)—as in *pratidivabhyām*.

This very point is explained in the *Prakriyākaumudī* and other works (Pāṇini 8.2.2). Others, however, maintain that the Visarga of *na* in *pratidvin* becomes *viṣṇu-sarga* at the end of the word *viṣṇupada*, resulting in *pratidivāḥ* and *pratidivobhyām*. ||117||
118. In the case of *pathin*, *mathin*, and *ṛbhukṣin*, there is the elision of the *n* before the nominative suffix *su*.

119. For *pathin* and the others, *irāma* is substituted for *ārāma*; *kṛṣṇa* takes the place of *sthāna*, and *nuk* is inserted before the *th*. [This is based on the rules: "Not at the end of a word ending in *viṣṇu*" (Viṣṇuprakāśa 84), and "In *viṣṇucakra*, *hariveṇu*" (Sārasvataprakriyā 114). Here, even in the Nāgarī script, that which is called *viṣṇucakra* when it does not end in *viṣṇu* is not appropriate.
panthāḥ, panthānau, panthānaḥ, panthānam, panthānau ||118119||
120. Regarding *pathy* and so forth, there is the removal of the *bhagavatī* [suffix].
From the path by the path.
Because of the restriction everywhere by the word "only" (*eva*), according to [the rule] *nāmāntasya nasya haraḥ* (Viṣṇupurāṇa-vivaraṇa 115), by that—
pathibhyām, pathibhiḥ;
likewise,
manthāḥ, manthānau, manthānaḥ.
Ṛbhukṣāḥ, Ṛbhukṣāṇau, Ṛbhukṣāṇaḥ. ||120||
Now, regarding *śārṅgin*:
according to the rule *inhanpūṣanaryamanityeṣām uddhavasya*, the substitution of *trivikrama* (guṇa) occurs only for the *u*-vowel of *suśvin*.
Thus: *śārṅgī*, *śārṅgiṇau*, *śārṅgiṇaḥ*.
śārṅgiṇam, śārṅgiṇau, śārṅgiṇaḥ; śārṅgibhyām; he śārṅgin!
Likewise for vanamālin, halin, and daṇḍin.

The root *han* means "to kill. From it: *kaṃsahan* (nominative singular), *kaṃsahā* (instrumental singular), *kaṃsahanau* (nominative/accusative dual), *kaṃsahanaḥ* (nominative plural), *kaṃsahanam* (accusative singular), *kaṃsahanau* (accusative dual). ||121||
"Devoid of association with the non-existent" (*vamasatsaṅgahīnasya*)—thus [is] the removal of *ra* and *ma*.
122. *hanaḥ hasya gho ṇinnayoḥ*: [The substitute *gh* occurs for the *ha* of *han* when followed by a *ṇit* or *nit* suffix.
*kaṃsaghnaḥ*; *kaṃsaghnā*, *kaṃsaghnābhyām*.
ṅau—*kaṃsahani*, *kaṃsaghni*.
O *kaṃsahan*!
Thus,
pūṣā, pūṣaṇau, pūṣaṇaḥ;
pūṣaṇam, pūṣaṇau, pūṣṇaḥ;
pūṣṇi, pūṣaṇi.
According to some, [the form] is *pūṣaṇ*.

*Aryamā*, *aryamaṇau*. Numerical words beginning with *pañcan* always end in the plural and are identical in form across the three genders. According to the rule "from a numeral ending in *ṣaṇ* or *ka*" (*Vibhaktiprakriyā* 41), [the forms are]: *pañca*, *pañca*, *pañcabhiḥ*, *pañcabhyaḥ*. ||122||

123. After words ending in *raṣan* (r, ṣ, or n) and after numerals, the augment *nuṭ* is added before the case-ending *ām* when it expresses the same meaning as the base itself. 124. For a word ending in *n* that is derived from *tri-vikrama*, the augment *nuṭ* is added before the case-endings marked with *n* (*nām*). For example: *pañcānām*, *pañcasu*. Likewise: *saptan*, *aṣṭan*, *navan*, *daśan*.
125. Or, [the substitution occurs] among the eight forms of devotion to Viṣṇu.
126. Therefore, for *jas* and *śas*, there is *auś* in its own sense.
Since *ś* is an *it*, by the rule "that which has *ś* as an *it* replaces the whole," the substitute ending in *ś* is a replacement for the entire form.
Eight, eight; eight, eight;
by eight, by eight (*aṣṭābhiḥ*, *aṣṭabhiḥ*); from eight, from eight (*aṣṭābhyaḥ*, *aṣṭabhyaḥ*)—in both cases [the forms] are the same: of eight (*aṣṭānām*).

In the case of *aṣṭan*, it is exactly like *paramapañcan* and *paramāṣṭan*, and so forth. However, when its own meaning [of "eight"] is not intended—as in *priyapañcan* (one who loves five)—the forms are *priyapañcā*, *priyapañcānau*, *priyapañcānaḥ*; and in the vocative singular, *bhagavan*, the form is *priyapañcñaḥ*, and so on; and in the genitive plural, *priyapañcñām*.
Even when *aṣṭan* has another meaning [as a compound], the substitution of *āt* may optionally occur, but the substitution of *auś* does not.
In the vocative singular: *priyāṣṭe*, *priyāṣṭāṣṭau*, *priyāṣṭāḥ*—O Blessed One, like Viśvapāvat!
In the nominative plural: *priyāṣṭaḥ*. In the genitive plural: *priyāṣṭāṣṭānām*.
In the masculine (*pakṣe*): *priyāṣṭā*, *priyāṣṭānau*, *priyāṣṭānaḥ*;
in the vocative singular (*bhagavati*): *priyāṣṭo*; in the genitive plural (*āmi*): *priyāṣṭnām*.

*Arvan* becomes *arvat*. 127. For the word *arvan*, when it is not preceded by *ana*, [the substitution of] *arvat* occurs before the case-endings beginning with *su*, excluding the vocative singular (*su*).
There is the augment *num* for those [stems] that have *catur* as their penultimate element. 127.
128. For the *n* of a word situated in a group of consonants excluding the nine [nasals], there is no substitution of *ṇ*.
Examples: *arvantau*, *arvantaḥ*, *arvantam*, *arvantau*, *arvataḥ*.
*arvatā*, *arvadbhyām*, *he arvan!* But when preceded by the negative particle *nañ*: *anarvā*, *anarvāṇau*.
*kṛṣṇagup*; in the masculine: *kṛṣṇagup*, *kṛṣṇagub*, *kṛṣṇagupau* ||128||
Regarding the root *praśam*, its *m* becomes *n* before a masculine suffix ending in a Visarga (the "foot of Viṣṇu"), as well as before the suffixes *mat* and *vat*.

Here, there is a misconception regarding the rule *jhali ca* (Pāṇini 8.2.26). In forms such as *saṅgaṃsyate*, by the force of the specific injunction, only the substitution of *n* for *m* would occur. However, according to the indicative mark (*jñāpaka*) in the rule *praśāna praśāno nasya cādau* (Sārasvata-prakriyā 108), the elision (*hara*) of *n* does not take place. Thus: *praśāmau*, *praśāmaḥ*, *praśānbhyām*. ||129||

The word *catur* is always plural; in the masculine, for its place [where *su* would occur], there is *ām* after *catur* and *anaḍuh*, provided it is not preceded by *kṛṣṇa*; however, when *buddhi* follows, there is *am*.

The measured forms are *mita-*, *catvāraḥ*, and *caturaḥ*. When the suffix *visarga* is applied, it becomes *punā rarāmaḥ*—namely, *caturbhiḥ* and *caturbhyaḥ*. By the rule “*raṣaṇāntaḥ*” (*Viṣṇupurāṇa-prakriyā* 123), the augment *nuṭ* is added, resulting in *caturṇām*. ||130||
131. The suffix *snu* does not apply after *rarama* when followed by a case-ending (*sup*).

[Examples of] the four [cases]: *priyacatur—priyacatvāḥ*, *priyacatvārau*, *priyacatvāram*. Because it does not have its own meaning [as a primary noun], there is no insertion of *nuṭ* before the genitive plural ending *ām*: *priyacaturām*. O *he priyacatvaḥ!* [The word] *hal* in the locative plural is *halṣu*. From the root *abhr* with the *kvip* suffix, the word *abhra* takes the nominative singular *su*; according to the rule "in the presence of *sat* [the suffix *kvip*] is elided," it becomes *apabha*. However, regarding that [rule], the prohibition of *ṣaṇa* is stated as an option.
From the causative form of the root *cakṣ* (to speak) with the prefix *vi-* (*vicaṣṭe*), the suffix *kvip* is applied according to the rule "daityavṛścamācaṣṭe": thus, *daityab*, *daityabau*. ||131||

132. *Hara* [is substituted] for *yava* ending in *viṣṇupada* when *gopāla* follows; and *hara* for *nava* when *hari* follows (*Viṣṇupurāṇa-prakriyā* 115)—as in *daityabhyām*, *daityabhiḥ*, *daityapsu*. 132.
133. However, when *sarva* is the sovereign [first member], there is an option; but when *hari* is present, there is no sandhi. Thus: *daityabāyāti* may be either *daitya āyāti* or *daityabāyāti*.

From the root *pracch*, with the suffix *kvip*, ending in *śar* and *mā*, we have *kṛṣṇaprāś*: some say the forms are *kṛṣṇaprāṭ*, *kṛṣṇaprāśau*, and *kṛṣṇaprācchau*. Similarly, from *vāñch*, we have *vānś*; because the rule for *hari* is obligatory, the forms are *vān*, *vāṃśau*, and *vāṃśaḥ*; some say *vāñchau*. From *kṛṣṇaspṛś*, the forms are *kṛṣṇaspṛk* and *kṛṣṇaspṛśau*. But when preceded by *udak*, it is *udakaspṛṭ*.

*ṣarāmānto dadhṛdh-*: *dadhṛk*, *dadhṛṣau*, *dadhṛṣaḥ*. *kaṃsadviṣ-*: by the rule *yasya ḍaḥ* (Viṣamapadaprakaraṇa 105), [the final *ṣ* becomes *ṭ*], resulting in *kaṃsadviṭ* and *kaṃsadviḍ*; [the forms are] *kaṃsadviṣau*. *ṣaṣ* is always plural. By the rule *ṣanānta* (Viṣamapadaprakaraṇa 41), [the *ṣ* becomes *ḍ*]: *ṣaḍ*, *ṣaḍbhiḥ*, *ṣaḍbhyaḥ*. ||133||

In the case of *raṣanānta* (Vipra 123), the augment *nuṭ* is applied; then, by *ṣasya ḍaḥ* (Vipra 105), the *ṣ* becomes *ḍ*. 134. Regarding the rule for *hariveṇu*, there is a constant application [of the suffix] when *pratyaya* and *hariveṇu* follow.
The error lies in thinking that this applies only when *mayaṭ* follows. 134.

135. After the letter *ṣ*, the dental class (*tavarga*) followed by a letter of the retroflex class (*ṭavarga*) is replaced by the retroflex class; however, this does not apply when the *ṭavarga* follows a word ending in *viṣṇu-pada*, nor in the case of the words *nāman*, *navati*, and *nagarī*. Consequently, there is retroflexity for the *ṭavarga* in *nāman*: *ṣaṇṇām*, *ṣaṭsu*. There is retroflexity for the *ṭavarga* in *navati* and *nagarī*: *ṣaṇṇavatiḥ*, *ṣaḍṇavatiḥ*; *ṣaṇṇagaryaḥ*, *ṣaḍṇagaryaḥ*. It does not occur here: *ṣannaraḥ*, *ṣaḍnaraḥ*; *ṣannāvaḥ*, *ṣaḍnāvaḥ*.

However, rules such as *datau paravarṇau* (Saṃskṛtaprakāśa 102) are stated separately merely for the sake of easily understanding euphonic combinations (*sandhi*). The purpose of including the term "end of the word *viṣṇu*" in rules such as *na tu viṣṇupadāntāt* will be demonstrated in examples like *ghaṭṭiḥ* (Kṛtprakriyā 437).
This is because [the former rules] would lack their own specific meaning [otherwise]; for example: *priyaṣaṣaḥ*, *priyaṣaṣām*. (135)

*Sajuṣ*—136. In the presence of *sajuṣ* and *āśis*, the letter *r* replaces the final *is* or *us* of a verbal root when followed by a word ending in *viṣṇu* (a case-ending); furthermore, the *viṣṇu-sarga* (the visarga representing *r*) is substituted for that [root-final *r*] before a *sup* (case-ending). The purpose of mentioning "verbal root" (*dhātu*) is to provide for the substitution of *ṣ* in the formation of compounds, as will be explained in the section on compound operations (Samāsapradīpa 328) regarding the example *sarpiṣkāmyati*. ||136||
137. From the root *sajus*, [the forms are]: *sajuḥ*, *sajuṣau*, *sajūrbhyām*;

*sajuṣṣu* (with *ṣatva*); *śauritvaṃ sajūṣṣu*. From the desiderative root (*sanantadhātu*) with *kvip*: *pipaṭhiṣ*. Because it ends in *viṣṇupada* (a word ending in *-i*), the cause for [the application of] *ṣatva* ceases, and thus *ṣatva* is lost. [The forms are]: *pipaṭhīḥ*, *pipaṭhiṣau*, *pipaṭhiṣaḥ*; *pipaṭhīrbhyām*, *pipaṭhīṣu*. Similarly, *viśvacikīrṣa*. According to the rule *rāt sasyaiva* (Viṣṇupadaprakāśa 110), [the forms are]: *viśvacikīḥ*, *viśvacikīrṣau*, *viśvacikīrbhyām*, *viśvacikīrṣu*.

138. For *sahaja* and for [words] related to *kara* and *rāma* ending in *-am*, when the suffixes beginning with *sat* (i.e., case endings) follow, *ḍa* is substituted; what need is there to mention others? This also applies to words derived from roots preceded by *diś*, *dṛś*, *anu*, *dak*, *pūrva*, *spṛś*, and *jā*. In that regard, for *sahaja*: *gorakṣ—goraṭ-goraḍ*, *gorakṣau*, *gorakṣaḥ*, *goraḍbhyām*, *goraṭsu*.

139. Some say that *rakṣ* optionally takes *ka*. Thus: *gorakṣ*. In the case of roots beginning with a retroflex (*mūrdhanya*), such as *viś* and *viṣ*, when followed by the desiderative suffix (*san*): one who wishes to enter is *vivikṣ*—[yielding] *viviṭ*, *viviḍ*, *vivikṣau*, *vivikṣaḥ*. From the root *vah*, in the sense of "one who wishes to carry" (*voḍhum icchati*), it is *vivaṭ* or *vivaḍ*, *vivakṣau*, *vivakṣaḥ*. But for others—that is, from the root *vac*—it is *vivak*—[yielding] *vivag*, *vivakṣau*. From the root *dah*, [the form] *didhakṣ* yields *didhak* or *didhag*, *didhakṣau*, *didhakṣaḥ*. For *diś* and the others, [the forms are] *didik*, *didṛk*, *pispṛk*. And this is what the followers of Pāṇini maintain.

The *Kālāpas* state that there is elision of any [suffix] other than one in place of the letter *gh* or the *ca*-group, even if it is in place of *ṣ*, *ḍh*, and so on. Therefore, they say *vivīḥ*. From the root *pis*, [the forms] are *supis* (ending in *sarāmānta*), *supīḥ*, *supisau*, *supisaḥ*; from the root *tus*, *sutus*—*sutūḥ*, *sutusau*, *sutusaḥ*. Regarding the substitution of *ṣ*: *supīḥṣu*, *sutuḥṣu*.

For *ūruśravas*, Trivikrama says by the rule *atvasantoddhavasya* (Vipraprakaṣa 111): *ūruśravāḥ*, *ūruśravasau*, *ūruśravasaḥ*; *ūruśravobhyām*, *ūruśravaḥsu*; *he ūruśravaḥ!* Similarly for *viṣṭaraśravas*, *vedhas*, and so forth.
Now, ending with the suffixes *doṣū* and so forth: *doḥ*, *doṣau*, *doṣaḥ*; *doṣam*, *doṣau*. ||139||
140. *Doṣ* [is substituted] for *doṣan* when followed by case endings beginning with a vowel (*ya*) or a consonant (*nu*).
According to the rule *vamasatsaṅga* (Viśvapradīpa 89), there is the elision of *ra* by *arāmaharaḥ*—[thus we have] *doṣṇaḥ*, *doṣaḥ*; *doṣṇā*, *doṣā*, *dorbhyām*, *doṣabhyām*, and so forth.

[In the compound] *pītavastraḥ* (one who wears yellow garments)—meaning he wears (*vas-te*) what is yellow (*pītam*)—there is the absence of *trivikrama* (the substitution of *t* for *s*) according to the rule *dhātuṃ vinā* (Viśvapradīpa 111)—[resulting in] *pītavaḥ*, *pītavasau*.

"Kaṃsahiṃsa" means "one who destroys Kaṃsa. Because it is listed in the intermediate section [of the sūtras], Viṣṇu possesses both the status of the Lord of All (*sarveśvaratva*) and the status of being born from Viṣṇu (*viṣṇujanatva*); thus, due to its association with the virtuous (*satsaṅga*), there is the elision of the *s*. Since it is a cause for the application of the rule, it is indeed *nara-āma* (the name Nara). Due to the specific qualification "excluding verbal roots" (*dhātu-varjita*, Viṣṇupurāṇa-prakriyā 82), Trivikrama does not apply here: *kaṃsahin*, *kaṃsahiṃsau*, *kaṃsahinbhyām*. However, in the case of the rule prescribing effort (*yatna-vidhi*), only the Viṣṇucakra is taken as the substitute for *num*; therefore, there is no substitution of *ṣ* here: *kaṃsahinsu*. ||140||
Regarding *vaikuṇṭhadhvas*:

in the rule *dhvaṃsu-śraṃsu-vasvanaḍuhāṃ do viṣṇupadānte* (Pāṇini 8.2.71), there is a misconception that the *jhali ca* (Pāṇini 8.2.26) rule applies here, leading to the error seen in forms such as *dhvasta*. The roots *dhvaṃsu* and *śraṃsu* have the *anubandha* *c* attached to them; this status of having *c* as an *anubandha* is understood only in their nominal state (*nāma-avasthā*). Because of the inclusion of *ac* [in the rule], the augment *num* does not apply here: *vaikuṇṭhadhvat*, *vaikuṇṭhadhvasau*, *vaikuṇṭhadhvadbhyām*. Likewise for *vaikuṇṭhaśrat*.

Here, the *vasu* suffix [is applied]: *vidvasu*. Because it is marked with *u* (*uditatvāt*) and because of the connection with the four arms (*caturbhuja-anubandha*), there is the insertion of *nuṃ* (Pāṇini 7.1.70); and by the rule "ending in *n*" (*nānta*, Viśvapriya 82), we have *trivikrama*; and by the rule "removal of the final *s* when followed by *sat-saṅga*" (*satsaṅgāntahara*, Viśvapriya 96), we have: *vidvān*, *vidvāṃsau*, *vidvāṃsaḥ*; *vidvāṃsam*, *vidvāṃsau*. ||141||

142. *Vasuḥ*, *vasya*, *ur*, *bhagavati*. The term *vasya* is an elliptical reference (*sārāmanirdeśaḥ*). Regarding the substitution of *ṣ*: *viduṣaḥ*, *viduṣā*, *vidvadbhyām*, *vidvadbhiḥ*, *viduṣe*, *he vidvan!* The forms beginning with *ād-vas-* will be established in the section on *kṛdanta* (5.20). The forms are as follows: *Vasuḥ* (masculine nominative singular): Derived from the root *vas* ("to dwell") with the suffix *u*; the final *u* is replaced by *o*, which becomes *au* before the case-ending *su*. *Vasya* (masculine genitive singular): Derived from the same root; the suffix *ya* is added, and the vowel is lengthened. *Ur* (neuter nominative/accusative singular): Derived from the root *vṛ* ("to choose"); the suffix *u* is added, and the vowel is lengthened. *Bhagavati* (feminine locative singular): Derived from the root *bhaj* ("to worship"); the suffix *gavan* is added, followed by the feminine suffix *ī* and the locative ending *i*. The forms for the word *vidvas* ("wise") are as follows: Nominative plural: *vidvāṃsaḥ* Accusative plural: *viduṣaḥ* Instrumental singular: *viduṣā* Instrumental dual: *vidvadbhyām* Instrumental plural: *vidvadbhiḥ* Dative singular: *viduṣe* Vocative singular: *he vidvan!* The forms beginning with *ād-vas-* will be explained in the *kṛdanta* section (5.20). The specific forms are as follows: [list of forms].
ādivān, ādivāṃsau, ādivāṃsaḥ; ādivaṃsam, ādivaṃsau, āduṣaḥ; āduṣā, ādivadbhyām...
Likewise for *jakṣivān*: then *jagmivān*—namely, *jagmivān*, *jagmivāṃsau*, *jagmivāṃsaḥ*;
*jagmivāṃsam*, *jagmivāṃsau*.
Likewise, from the root *gam* (to go):
*jaganvān*, *jaganvāṃsau*, *jaganvāṃsaḥ*. In both cases, for the word *bhagavat*: *jagmuṣaḥ*, and so forth. ||142||

Regarding *puṃsaḥ*: 143. In the case of *puṃsaḥ*, [the form] *pumān* occurs in place of *kṛṣṇa*. Here, there is a misconception that the rule applies when *suṭ* [is present], according to Pāṇini 7.1.89. Furthermore, if [the term] were applied figuratively (*gauṇatva*) to Brahman, there would be a fault. [The form is] *urāmaḥ*.
pumān, pumāṃsau, pumāṃsaḥ; pumāṃsam, pumāṃsau, puṃsaḥ; puṃsā, puṃbhyām...

The authors of the *Bhāṣāvṛtti* and others maintain that every anusvāra is perceived as *num*. In this regard, a prohibition of the *ṣatva* [substitution] must be stated for this *uṇādi*-derived word in forms such as *puṃsaḥ*; however, *ṣatva* does apply here in the form *puṃṣu*. Others say "no"—thus *puṃsu*.
For *uśanas*, the forms are *uśanā*, *uśanasau*, *uśanasaḥ* ||143||
144. For *uśanas*, there is the absence of the final nasal (*n*), the elision of the *s* (*salopa*), and for *buddha*, the presence of the *visarga* at the end.

Thus: *he uśanan*, *he uśana*, *he uśanaḥ*. Likewise, *anehā*, *anehasau*; *purudaṃśā*, *purudaṃśasau*; *he anehaḥ*, *he purudaṃśaḥ*. However, forms such as *śvetavāh*, *puroḍāś*, *ukthaśāsa*, and so forth, are Vedic (*chāndasa*). [Also] *kṛṣṇavāh*.

145. For *has*, [the substitute] is *ḍha*; for *nah*, it is *dha*; but for a root beginning with *da*, it is *gha*. For the roots *druh*, *muh*, *hana*, *śas*, *nuh*, and *snih*, [the substitution is optional] at the end of a *viṣṇupada* (pada ending in a case-suffix) and before a *vaiṣṇava* (suffix beginning with a case-suffix). All these are roots. [Examples: *kṛṣṇavāṭ* / *kṛṣṇavāḍ*, *kṛṣṇavāhau*, *kṛṣṇavāhaḥ*.
146. Or "vāha" [is used] for "ūṭh," O Blessed One; it is established. ||145||

147. *Advayādūṭho vṛṣṇīndraḥ* (The Lord of the Vṛṣṇis, who is not separated from non-duality). *Kṛṣṇauhaḥ*. [In the forms] *kṛṣṇauhā*, *kṛṣṇavāḍbhyām*, [and] *kṛṣṇavāṭsu*, the rule *ṣaḍhoḥ kaḥ se* (Aṣṭādhyāyī 8.2.41) does not apply—both here and in the case of *kaṃsadviṭsu*—because by the absence of that [suffix], it pertains only to verbal roots (*dhātu*). Consequently, in cases such as *kṛṣṇavāṭsāt bhavati*, [the substitution] would not occur even when a *taddhita* suffix follows a *kṛdanta* root. Since this is a form accepted [by tradition], it must be resolved even by the followers of Pāṇini. Even though [Pāṇini] stated *asupi* (when not followed by a sup-suffix), this must indeed be resolved by Kramadīśvara and Padmanābha in the case of a *taddhita* suffix.
But Kṛṣṇapaṇḍita, having stated "at the end of a word," established everything accordingly. ||147||
Now, regarding *anaḍuh*: [the rule] *caturanaḍuhorām* (ViP 130)—148. *anaḍuho nuṃ ca sau* (Pāṇini 7.1.82).
By the rule *satsaṅgāntaharaḥ* (ViP 96), the *n* is elided; however, because it is not yet established (*asiddha*), there is no elision of the *n*.
anaḍvān, anuḍvāhau, anaḍvāhaḥ;
anaḍvāham, anuḍvāhau, anaḍuhaḥ; anaḍuhā, anaḍudbhyām.
O Anuḍvan! Regarding *buddhe* [in the locative case], according to the rule *goduh-javara-hari-gadādeḥ* (Viśvapradīpa 130, 114), etc., we have:
*godhuk*, *goduhau*, [and so on].

*godhugbhyām*, *godhukṣu*. Regarding the substitution of *gh* [for *dh*], the rule *dhātoḥ* (ViPRA 145) refers only to that which is original (*aupadeśika*); therefore, from the form *dāmaliṭ*, ending in *ky-aṅ* and followed by *kvip*—meaning "one who acts like Dāmaliṭ"—the form *kaṃsadruh-* [is derived].

*kaṃsadhruk*, *kaṃsadhruṭ*, *kaṃsadruhau*, *kaṃsadhrugbhyām*, *kaṃsadhruḍbhyām*; likewise *kṛṣṇamuṭ*, *kṛṣṇasnih*, and so forth. Regarding *kṛṣṇāṅghrilih*: by the rule "of *h* there is *ḍh*" (*vi.pra.* 145), [it becomes] *kṛṣṇāṅhriliḍ*, *kṛṣṇāṅghrilihau*. ||148||
turāsāh— 149. *sāḍhaḥ* becomes *ṣāṭ*.
[The forms are: turāṣāṭ (turāṣāḍ), turāsāhau, turāsāhaḥ, turāṣāḍbhyām. ||149||
Thus end the *liṅgas* of Puruṣottama ending with Viṣṇujana.
Those ending in "janā" belong to Viṣṇu, while those ending in "lakṣmī" are Liṅgas;
therein, the words ending in "carām" are Ṛks. Regarding the *c*-group (*cavarga*), as stated in the *Viṣṇuprādurbhāva* (97):
*ṛk*, *ṛcau*, *ṛcaḥ*.
From *ṛc* we have *ṛgbhyām* and *ṛkṣu*; likewise for *tvac*, *vāc*, *sraj*, *diś*, *dṛś*, and so forth—
e.g., *sraj*, *srajau*, *srajaḥ*.
*samidh*— *samit*, *samidau*, *samidaḥ*;
*sīman*— *sīmā*, *sīmānau*, *sīmānaḥ*.

Regarding *sīmā*: by the rule "optionally before the locative suffix *iṅ* and the genitive-locative suffix *ī*" (*Viśvapradīpa* 89), we have *sīmni* or *sīmani*. It is invariably plural. According to Trivikrama’s rule "ending in *n*" (*Viśvapradīpa* 82): *āpaḥ*, *apaḥ*.
150. [The suffixes] *do* and *bhe* [are applied after the word *ap*]. Examples:
*adbhiḥ*, *apsu*, *he āpaḥ*! Because [the word ends in] *tadanta* (that which ends in *ap*), there are forms such as *svadbhiḥ*, etc.
*Kakubh*—
*kakup*, *kakub*, *kakubhau*, *kakubbhyām*, *kakupsu*. Regarding *gir*: according to [Viśvaprasāda] 137, for a verbal root ending in *ir* or *ur*—*gīḥ*, *girau*, *giraḥ*.
In the case of *gīḥ*, [the forms are] *gīrbhyām* and *gīṣu*.
Likewise for *pur*: *pur*, *purau*, *puraḥ*.
In the feminine, *catur* takes the substitute *catasṛ* (Viṣamapadaprakāśa 71).

catasraḥ, catasraḥ, catasṛbhiḥ, catasṛbhyaḥ, catasṛṇām, catasṛṣu. Due to the specific rule "lakṣmīsthayoḥ" (Viśvapradīpa 71), these respective substitutes occur even when the compound as a whole possesses a different gender. For example: *priyāstisro yasya saḥ* (he to whom three beloveds belong).
priyatisā, priyatisrau, priyatisraḥ;
priyacatasā, priyacatasrau, priyacatasraḥ [in the cases of] ṅasi and ṅas.
In *priyatisraḥ*, *priyacatasraḥ*,
and *priyatisṛṇām*, when the entire measure [of the stem] constitutes the feminine suffix (*lakṣmītva*), the forms are *priyatriḥ*, *priyatrī*, and *priyatrayaḥ*. ||150||
div— 151. *div* [is substituted] before the nominative-accusative dual ending *au*.
*dyauḥ*, *divau*, *divaḥ*.
divam, divau, divaḥ,
152. After *div*, [the suffix] *ur* is substituted [for the case endings], except before the word *viṣṇupada*.
[Examples: *dyubhyām*, *dyuṣu*.
*diś*—

*dik*, *diśau*, *digbhyām*, *dikṣu*. Likewise for *dṛś*, *aghadviṣ*, and *kaṃsadviṭ* (the latter two ending in *vat*). Similarly for *vipruṣ*. Now, for *āśis*, by the rule beginning with *sajuṣ* (Vipraprabodha 136), [the final *s*] becomes *r*: *āśīḥ*, *āśiṣau*, *āśiṣaḥ*; *āśīrbhyām*, *āśīḥṣu*.
*uṣṇih*—*uṣṇik*, *uṣṇig*, *uṣṇihau*;
*upānah*—by the rule *naho dhaḥ* (ViPRA 145), [it becomes] *upānat* (*upānad*), *upānahau*. ||152||
Thus end the marks of Lakṣmī ending with the followers of Viṣṇu.
Those ending with Viṣṇujana are Brahma-lingas;
therein also [the forms] *pratyak*, *pratīcī*, and *pratyañci*.
*pratīc*, *pratyagbhyām*;
likewise, *prāc*: *prāṅ*, *prāñcī*, *prāñci*.
As for the words *pratyañc* and *prāñc*: *pratyaṅ*, *pratyañcī*, *pratyañci*.

In the nominative plural (*śas*), two instances of *ñarām* should be written. However, when *ñarām* occurs in place of *mit*, the *nuṃ* augment is not seen, as in *kaṃsahiṃso brahmaṇi kaṃsahiṃsīti*—there would be only the discus of Viṣṇu [the *ñarām*].
*Tiryac*: *tiryak*, *tiraścī*, *tiryañci*.
*Ūrj*: *ūrk*, *ūrjī*, *ūnarji*.
153. Regarding *bahūrj*, there is a prohibition of the augment *num*.
[The forms are] *bahūrji*. Some desire the *num* augment to be placed before the final vowel—[thus] *bahūrjī*.

*Jagat*—*jagat*, *jagatī*, *jaganti*. Now, those ending in the *śatṛ* suffix: *bhavatṛ*—*bhavataḥ*. Regarding the *numī* suffix, it will be explained in the section on *kṛdanta* (5.17): *bhavantī*, *bhavanti*. There is an option for *tudatṛ*, *bhātṛ*, *kaviṣyatṛ*, and so forth: *tudat*, *tudatī*, *tudantī*, *tudanti*. Likewise: *bhāt*, *bhātī*, *bhānti*; *kariṣyat*, *kariṣyatī*, *kariṣyantī*, *kariṣyanti*.

The word *mahat*: *mahat*, *mahatī*, *mahānti*. *Brahman*: *brahma*. Because of the qualifying attribute "of one devoid of association with the great and the small" (*vamasatsaṅgahīnasya*, Viṣṇupurāṇa 89), there is no shortening of the vowel: *brahmaṇī*, *brahmaṇi*, *brahmaṇā*, *brahmabhyām*. ||153||
154. *nasya* is substituted for *haḥ* when followed by *brahmaṇi* or *buddhe*.
O *brahma*, O *brahman*! Likewise in *śarman*, *varman*, and *carman*. 154.

Now, *ahan*—155. The form *ahnaḥ* occurs at the end of a compound with *viṣṇu*, as in *viṣṇvahnaḥ*. It should be stated that [the substitution of *t* for *n*] does not apply when the word is masculine. Thus: *ahaḥ*. But in the dual and plural, there is optionally [the substitution of *t* for *n*] according to Viśvarūpa’s Prakriyā (89); however, because they lack the status of verbal roots (*dhātu*), there is no change to *gh*. Thus: *ahnī*, *ahanī*, *ahāni*, *ahnā*. ||155||

156. In this case, the substitution of *ra* (repha) must be stated even when there is an absence of a suffix (*svādyabhāva*). [Examples: *ahobhyām*. Even when [the word] is understood—as in "O Day! (*he ahaḥ*)—in a compound, it is masculine, namely *trivikrama*, and not the neuter form of Viṣṇu: *dīrghāhā nidāghaḥ*. But when it is understood [as a vocative], it is *he dīrghāhan!*; here, the substitution of *ṇa* must be stated: *dīrghahāṇau*, *dīrghāhāṇaḥ*, *dīrghāhṇaḥ*.

[The forms of] *supathin*: *supathi*, *supathī*, *supanthāni*. And in the *śas* [case]: *supanthāni*. There is a misconception regarding the rule that "for *pathin* and others, *num* is inserted before *su*" (*pathyādīnāṃ suṭi num*).

*dṛṣṭaśārṅgin*—*dṛṣṭaśārṅgi*, *dṛṣṭaśārṅgiṇī*, *dṛṣṭaśārṅgīṇi*. Similarly, *dṛṣṭakaṃsah*—*dṛṣṭakaṃsaha*, *dṛṣṭakaṃsahanī*, *dṛṣṭakaṃsaghnī*, *dṛṣṭakaṃsahāni*. Likewise, *dṛṣṭapūṣan*, *dṛṣṭāryaman*. According to Trivikrama: "After roots ending in *n*, except for *svap*" (*vi.pra.* 89)—*svāmpi*, *svadbhyām*.
*Vār*—*vāḥ*, *vārī*, *vāri*. Even after words other than *īśvara*, [the suffix] *rarāmajaḥ* [is applied] (*sa.pra.* 145)—*vārbhyām*.
Here too, there are four forms: *payas*—namely, *payas*, *payasī*, *payāṃsi*, and *payobhyām*.

*Havis*—*haviḥ*. This suffix is derived from the *Uṇādi* [list] as *sarām*; therefore, there is the substitution of *ṣ*—*haviṣī*, *havīṃṣi*, *haviṣbhyām*. With the *viṣṇusarga* (the *visarga* of Viṣṇu), there is the substitution of *ṣ*: *haviḥṣu*; with the *śauritva* (the *ṣ* of Śauri): *haviṣṣu*. Similarly for *dhanus*. After *atipuṃs*: *atipum*, *atipuṃsī*, *atipumāṃsi*.
svanaḍuh—svanaḍut, svanaḍuhī, svanaḍvāṃhi ||156||
Thus end the Brahma-liṅgas, ending with Viṣṇu’s attendants.
Thus, the three genders have been demonstrated.
Now, regarding words whose gender is determined by their qualifiers (viśeṣaṇaliṅga):
here, words such as *kṛṣṇa* and others are fixed [in gender] when used as proper names (*saṃjñā*) or in specific senses, such as *puruṣottama*.

158. Words such as *saṅkhyā* (number) and others take the gender of the word they denote (*vācyaliṅga*). 159. Those that function as adjectives in grammatical apposition (*samānādhikaraṇa*) take the gender, number, and case of the substantive (*viśeṣya*) they qualify. 160. That through the medium of which a distinction is expressed—whether by way of genus (*jāti*), quality (*guṇa*), or action (*kriyā*)—is the substantive (*viśeṣya*). That by which its distinction is expressed is the adjective (*viśeṣaṇa*).

For example: "Kṛṣṇa is a cowherd," "Rādhā is a cowherd-maiden," "the garment is made of linen," "Kṛṣṇa is dark-complexioned," "Rādhā is fair-complexioned," "the garment is yellow," "Kṛṣṇa is playful," "Rādhā is playful," "Gokula is a place of play," and so forth.
161. An indeclinable functions as an adjective, as in: *mahatsvaḥ* (great heaven).

For example: "O Kṛṣṇa! I am yours" (*he kṛṣṇa! tavāham*) and "O Rāma and Kṛṣṇa! I am yours" (*he rāmakṛṣṇau! yuvayoraham*). How then can I compose what is appropriate for you, O Goddess? This is because, even though the vocative is treated as non-existent, the preceding word remains existent (*sattvāt*). ||209||

210. When there are vocatives expressing a common meaning and sharing the same grammatical locus, if they are situated in their proper sequence, the one that precedes [the other] retains its original accent.
211. And optionally so in the plural.

In this regard, there are substitutes (*ādeśa*). [Example: "O Vaiṣṇava, Kṛṣṇa is dear to you. Here, *vaiṣṇava* is a general term meaning "one who possesses love for Him" as well as "one who is devoid of it," while those two [forms] are its specific referents (*viśeṣya*). In that case, when there is a subsequent reference (*anvādeśa*), the substitutes are obligatory; however, when there is no subsequent reference (*ananvādeśa*), they are optional. Why specify "general term"? [Counter-example: "O Brahmarāta, O Kṛṣṇajña, Kṛṣṇa is yours. Since *brahmarāta* is the name of a single individual, it is not a general term.

Therefore, both [forms] are treated as if non-existent according to the sūtra numbered 209. Thus: *hare kṛpālo 'smān pāhi*. In the plural: *vaiṣṇavāḥ śrībhāgavatajñāḥ*, [the forms] *ru* and *vaḥ* [are used for] *kṛṣṇaḥ*, or for "you" (*yuṣmākam*). These substitutes (*ādeśāḥ*) apply even when there is no subsequent reference (*ananvādeśe*). This is the system of Pāṇini based on grammatical derivation (*prakriyā*). There is, however, no great difference [between this and other systems]. For instance, those three sūtras are: "An address (*āmantritam*) preceding [another word] is treated as if non-existent" (Pā. 8.1.72).

[These rules are: Pāṇini 8.1.72, “Not [is the substitution of *bhavat* applied] when followed by an addressed word in grammatical apposition that expresses a general term” (sāmānyavacana); and 8.1.74, “When followed by an addressed word expressing a specific term, the plural [of *bhavat*] is optionally [retained]. In these rules beginning with “when addressed” (*āmantrite*), the locative case is indeed one of subsequent reference (*parasaptamī*). In the middle rule, because the non-existence of the general term is negated, the substitutions are based on that very fact. In the final rule, however, because of the optionality of that [negation], there is an optionality of those [substitutions]. The word *bhavatu* denotes the second person pronoun (*yuṣmad*), just like the word *bhagavatu*. 210–211.
Now, regarding the word *kim*: 212. In the sense of devotion to Viṣṇu, the substitute *ka* replaces *kim*, even when it follows a prefix.

[The forms are: *kaḥ*, *kau*, *ke*; *kam*, *kau*, *kān*—just like *sarva*. In a secondary derivative (*taddhita*) following the fifth case (ablative), [the form is] *kutaḥ*. In the seventh case (locative)—*kva*? *kutra*? ||212||

Now, an illustration of the feminine suffix *lakṣmī* as a marker for names ending in *kṛṣṇa*: 213. For *kṛṣṇanāmā*, [the nominative singular] is *rādhā*; for the plural, *vṛṣṇiṣu*; and for the preceding [stem], *vāmanaḥ*. In the case of *pit* (genitive singular), it is *sarvasyai*; in *ṅasi*, *sarvasyāḥ*; in *ṅas*, *sarvasyāḥ*. In *āmi*, by the rule *kṛṣṇanāma* (Viṣṇupurāṇa 170), there is *suṭ*, resulting in *sarvāsām*. In *ṅi*, by the rule *nīrādhābhyāṃ ṅerām* (Viṣṇupurāṇa 51), it becomes *sarvasyām*. In the case of secondary suffixes (*taddhita*), it is as before. Thus are *viśvā* and others. 213.

214. In a *dig-bahuvrīhi* compound, there is optionally the designation "kṛṣṇanāman" [for the first member]. Thus: *uttarapūrva*, *uttarapūrvāyai*. When the seven beginning with that [feminine suffix] are applied to the garden of *saṃsāra*, then for those beginning with *tad*, *taḥ* becomes *saḥ* in the nominative singular (*sau*). Thus: *sā*, *te*, *tāḥ*; *tām*, *te*, *tāḥ*. Likewise for *yad*: *yā*, *ye*, *yāḥ*. For *etad*: *eṣā*, *ete*, *etāḥ*. For *idam*, however, in the sense of Lakṣmī: *iyam*, *ime*, *imāḥ*; *imām*, *ime*, *imāḥ*. In the eight cases other than the nominative singular (*soḥ*), for *idam* that does not end in *ka*, *anaṣ* is substituted. Thus: *anayā*. In the Vaiṣṇava [system], however, it is *aś*. Thus: *ābhyām*, *ābhiḥ*.

*asyai*, *asyāḥ*. [By *suṭ* (Vi. Pra. 170) and *aś* (Vi. Pra. 186)], followed by *āp*: *āsām*. For the word *adas*, in the nominative singular (*sau*), it is treated like a masculine: *asau*. And for the *da*, there is *ma* (Vi. Pra. 183): *amū*, *amūḥ*. *amūm*, *amū*, *amūḥ*. *amuyā*, *amūbhyām*, *amūbhiḥ*. According to Vāmana (Vi. Pra. 213), in the feminine and neuter genders, there is optionally the substitution of the preceding [vowel]: *amuṣyai*, *amūbhyām*, *amūbhyaḥ*. *amuṣyāḥ*, *amūbhyām*, *amūbhyaḥ*. *amūṣyāḥ*, *amūyoḥ*, *amūṣām*. *amūṣyām*, *amūyoḥ*, *amūṣu*.
Like *sarva* and other [pronominals]. For the word *dvi*: *dve*, *dve*, *dvābhyām*, *dvābhyām*, *dvābhyām*, *dvayoḥ*, *dvayoḥ*.
From the word *bhavat* etc.: *bhavatī*, *bhavatyau*.
For the word *kim*: *kā*, *ke*, *kāḥ*. Like *sarva* and other [pronominals] ||214||
Now, regarding the neuter (*brahmali*):
*sarvam*, *sarve*, *sarvāṇi*. Again, like that [masculine]. From the third case onwards, like *puruṣottama*. *ubhau*, *ubhe*. 215.
After words beginning with *anya*, *tu* is substituted for the nominative-accusative singular (*svamoḥ*) in the neuter.
The forms *ukavitau* are established. *Anyat-anya*, *anye-anyāni*. Eleven words beginning with *anya*, excluding *ekatara*: *tat-te*, *tāni*; *idam*, *ime*, *imāni*. ||215||
216. In the case of the repetition of what has been stated regarding duality and singularity, the substitution of *enad* for *idam* and *etad* before a neuter [noun] is to be expressed.
*Etad gacchati* (this goes); *atho enat paśya* (and look at this).
When *adaḥ* remains as *ame*, then later—*amū*, *amūni*. Again, like that: *dve*, *dve*. *bhavat*, *bhavatī*, *bhavanti*. Again, like that: *kim*, *ke*, *kāni*. Again, like that. ||216||
217. After an indeclinable (*avyaya*), there is the elision of the case-endings beginning with *su* (the nominative singular).

Indeclinables include those beginning with *svar*, those beginning with *ca*, and those beginning with *vad*; furthermore, secondary suffixes (*taddhita*), the suffix *ktvā*, and verbal roots ending in *m* are also indeclinables. Indeed, indeclinables are both denoters (*vācaka*) and indicators (*dyotaka*). Among these, the denoters are *svaḥ*, *prātaḥ*, and so forth. For these, the very nature of Brahman constitutes the qualifier (*viśeṣaṇa*). Examples include: "beautiful heaven" (*sundaraḥ svaḥ*), "in beautiful heaven" (*sundare svaḥ*), and "beautiful heavens" (*sundarāṇi svaḥ*). In this regard, the misconception that there is only the singular number is erroneous; for duality and other numbers are unavoidable, and because the case-ending *su* is elided even after an indeclinable, there would be a contradiction [if one insisted on the absence of plurality].
Indicative particles (dyotaka) include: ca, vā, ha, aha, vai, tu, api, and so forth, as well as the group beginning with pra (prādayaḥ). ||217||

218. The particles beginning with *ca* are designated as *nipātas*. Since meanings are expressed through them by way of indication (*dyotakatayā*), they possess meaning; therefore, suffixes such as *svādi* (the nominal case endings) are produced after them, yet only the nominative singular remains. Examples include those ending in *vadādi* and *taddhita*: *harivat*, *kṛṣṇībhavati*, and so forth. Also, those ending in *ktvā* and *māntakṛt*: *kṛtvā*, *kartum*, *kāram*, *kāram*, and so on. Regarding *mahāharatvam*: [as in] *o au pāṇḍaveṣu* (Viṣṇupurāṇa 6.1), one should understand that *na*, *aho*, and so forth are also included. ||218||
Thus ends the section on the names of Kṛṣṇa.
Thus ends the second section, titled "The Case-endings of Viṣṇu," in the Vaiṣṇava grammar known as the *Śrī-Śrī-Harināmāmṛta*. 2.
